Backends and assemblers

Part I · 85 threads in 5 era slices, from Go 1.0 to Go 1.28. Each thread gives its design, then a per-release timeline of what landed (Done) and what was still open. Release labels in a timeline link to that release's page.

● = the thread had substantive commits in that cycle; hover for the stage summary, click to jump to it in the release page.

SIMD: the simd packages and their compiler support (Go 1.18–1.28)
Compiler SIMD type system, ABI and register-allocation support●●●SIMD types, vec/mask register classes, ABI passing, X15 zeroing, CPU-feature-aware block analysis and VEX encodings exist on master behind GOEXPERIMENT=simd (X15 whole-register zeroing is unconditional); RegMask widened beyond 64 bits for SVE predicates.
simdgen: the instruction-table-driven generator●●●lives in src/simd/archsimd/_gen (separate module) with simdgen, unify, tmplgen, wasmgen, midway, specgen, gentools; one go generate regenerates everything.
AMD64 archsimd API: AVX, AVX2 and AVX-512 operations●●●simd/archsimd provides 128/256/512-bit vectors on amd64 with operations that map to AVX/AVX2/AVX-512 instructions; experimental (GOEXPERIMENT=simd), not under Go 1 compatibility.
Mask representation, masked operations and merge peepholes●●●masks are opaque MaskNxM types in archsimd; amd64 uses K registers where AVX-512 is available and vector registers otherwise; arm64 SVE uses predicate registers; IfElse/Masked replace Merge.

ARM64 SVE: scalable vectors and predicate masks●minimum-viable archsimd SVE types and a growing op set (types_sve.go, ops_sve.go); scalable vector length capped at 32 bytes in model, mask loads/stores removed.

API shaping and renames before stabilisation●●●API still experimental; renames continue.
Emulation of missing instructions and test infrastructure●●●ops_emulated_.go per arch; generated test helpers.

Backends and assemblers (Go 1.0–1.6)

Reader: Claude Sonnet. Cites 1,322 of 1,498 commits in this slice; every non-noise commit is cited, plus 25 larger commits the noise filter had set aside, which a separate gap reader described. Skimmed the design-heavy messages; the ppc64 and nacl threads rest mostly on subject lines. About 500 small commits are cited in grouped items.

Release digest for this slice
  • Go 1.0 — Everything from the first 6g (2008) through the 2012 release: 6g, 8g and 5g become full compilers with a first generation of registerization and peephole optimization, complex numbers, ARM hardware float, and the C compilers/assemblers are imported from Plan 9/Inferno. Threads: per-architecture compilers, register allocator/peephole, C compilers, assemblers.
  • Go 1.1 — int becomes 64 bits on amd64; a long series of 6g/8g/5g code-quality changes (out-of-line panicindex, componentgen, rotates, SSE register use, GO386), the first GOEXPERIMENT, and explicit type information for locals. Threads: expression codegen, register allocator, C compilers.
  • Go 1.2 — Groundwork for precise GC: funcdata/pcdata, pointer maps from cc and gc, zeroing of pointers on entry, proginfo, portable optimizer code and temporary merging. Threads: pointer maps/liveness, register allocator.
  • Go 1.3 — liblink: assemblers and compilers emit machine code and a new object format; liveness-based stack maps; NaCl and amd64p32; Duff’s device in the runtime. Threads: liblink, pointer maps/liveness, NaCl, zeroing/copying.
  • Go 1.4 — Preparation for translation (c2go annotations), plan9/amd64 and nacl/arm in liblink, assembly-function stack maps, small-struct registerization. Threads: liblink, C compilers, stack maps.
  • Go 1.5 — The toolchain becomes Go: liblink to cmd/internal/obj, cmd/asm, all compilers and linkers translated, C compilers deleted, go tool compile/link; ppc64 and arm64 ports; shared-library codegen; frame pointers; portable cgen. Threads: C→Go, assemblers, obj normalisation, ppc64, arm64, PIC/TLS.
  • Go 1.6 — mips64 port; position-independent code on ppc64le, arm, arm64, 386; AVX/VEX assembler support and AVX2 runtime assembly; code layout split from object writing. Threads: mips64, PIC/TLS, assemblers, zeroing/copying.

Per-architecture compilers 6g/8g/5g/9g and the shared gc code generator

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: the Prog-list code generators were replaced by the SSA backend (1.7 onward, other area); in 1.6 they still existed as Go packages cmd/compile/internal/{amd64,x86,arm,arm64,ppc64,mips64} → continues as Register-based calling convention (ABIInternal) ports beyond amd64 and amd64 code generation and GOAMD64 microarchitecture levels (1.18+)

Continues in: Removal of the legacy backend and decoupling gc from the code generators (Go 1.7 → Go 1.9)

Design. The compiler was one front end (src/cmd/gc, C plus yacc) and one back-end directory per architecture, each a copy of the same structure: gsubr.c (instruction emission gins, regalloc/regfree, gmove, optoas mapping Go operators to machine opcodes), cgen.c (expression code generation: cgen, agen, bgen, sgen), ggen.c (calls, clearfat, divide, shift), galign.c, and reg.c/peep.c for the optimizer. Code generation was a Sethi-Ullman tree walk: ullman numbers decide evaluation order (0eda21a2fd made the minimum 1 so “not computed” and “trivial” differ), registers come from regalloc, and running out gives “out of registers” (made a fatal error rather than a recoverable path in 5g/8g in 1.4, c1c5d479bd). Many bug-fix commits are the same fix applied three times (6feb61325a, 7e144bcab0, 0b2353edcb, 46fcfdaa7d).

6g (amd64) came first (0cafb9ea3d; div/mod d83b994da6; shifts and multiplies f7753f1687; floating point 36bfd2a906). 8g (386) started as “minimal 8g” on 2009-03-31 (dc5b4678e2), grew 64-bit arithmetic through register pairs (a8e4ed6a3d, split into cgen64.c by ab3d40b271) and x87 float with float→integer conversions that emulate the x86 overflow results 1<<15/1<<31/1<<63 (a00bfb5b49). 5g (ARM) was copied from 6g on 2009-05-01 (eac5db7f4c), “rebooted” 2009-05-28 (63e1b714de), and stack splitting for ARM arrived in a grab-bag change (1ac2cfc720); function literals b4896b496e; hardware float came later (9c6df3ca13, after software float 69188ad9bb).

Shared logic was hoisted into cmd/gc over time: portable statement generation and signature generation (bac922c6e1, 5e792b6c09, d30285a6f5, 531f242f5d), static initialisation (62231e91d0, da49bfe664, moved to gc cb49a999d1), division by constants (34f76b5de5), the walk-pass division rewrite (4cc9de9147), proginfo tables (1.2), and in 1.5 the wholesale unification of cgen/regalloc (b115c35ee3, “cutting 5 copies to 1”; motivation: a following change would implement x.(*T) without a runtime call, now 5x easier). Alignment became explicit and per-type in 2010 (e7a0f67603, groundwork for max-field alignment, issue 482).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done:
    • 2008: 6g emits amd64 (0cafb9ea3d, d83b994da6, f7753f1687, 36bfd2a906, method/interface code 8231e94520); morestack magic number $a-b produced by 6g and 6c (3f982aeaf6); fat-copy and overlap fixes (30fd44cf9d).
    • 2009: 8g and 5g created and bootstrapped (dc5b4678e2, a8e4ed6a3d, 3aa006b8cd, eac5db7f4c, 63e1b714de, 190b5c9ad2, 4556c04d8b, 86987055a3, 6d0983ae46); nil-pointer checks in 8g (9dd2e1e30f); inline x[lo:] slicing (652f55672d, 9bf597a210, bf0130cc0f); Go types in the object symbol table (43f29e64a6); first attempt at bounds-check elimination for range and [256]array[byte] (fdb030d86f); 8g bounds failures call throwindex (dc30800c28).
    • 2010: complex numbers (426099f42e for 6g, f229c8b546 identical 6g/8g with 5g a stub, b0ad7a4268 5g regalloc for complex); string index inlined in all three (e48c0fb562); amd64 TLS moved to segment memory so R14/R15 return to the register pool (e473f42b2d); ARM hardware float (9c6df3ca13); O(1) string compare when lengths differ (30dd191171); dead code elided (410927d1ad).
    • 2011–Feb 2012: explicit alignments (e7a0f67603), inline append when len<cap (d6b2925923), compact stack frames (2ac375b2df, ARM 2ad42a8249, unified layout 5ddf6255a1), f() < g() order (bac8f18035), goto restrictions (7f4c5ea7d8), interface ==/!= fast-path on differing types (f91cc3bdbb, ~3x for err == io.EOF), correct boundary checks in all compilers (6ed2b6c47d), NOPTRBSS for large pointer-free data (5bcad92f07). Left open: 6g still had 32-bit int; 5g and 8g trailed 6g in code quality.
  • Go 1.1 — Done: user-visible int becomes 64-bit on amd64: the compiler first learns len/cap are int (650160e36a), then flips (10ea6519e4, assembly offsets converted mechanically). 6g may use R14/R15 (8f8640a057) and all 16 SSE registers (57ad05db15); 8g imports componentgen (ae0862c1ec; LEAL count for cmd/go 89774 → 47548), igen cases (f4e76d5e02), no address-of-slice for &s[i] (2de064b63c, acbe6c94d7 for 6g); panicindex out of line (fefae6eed1); contiguous loop layout (001b75c942); 5g backports of 6g constant-operand code (7b36acc4ac, ed0c5dd11f, bbccfddb84, 01ddc8bd9a, 905e8dfa27, d8008a9eef, 3dcc63f750, 5bdf40dcca, bdd9f29780); user-visible GO386=387|sse selects FPU flavour, default 387 (9afb34b42e); method values (d3c758d7d2); closures without runtime code generation (9f647288ef) after the indirect func-value representation (1903ad7189); explicit TYPE pseudo-instructions for locals (1d5dc4fd48). Left open: no auto-detection of SSE2 (commit: “no auto-detection is performed”).
  • Go 1.2 — Done: trampolines moved to portable code (1f51d27922, 31be5deae4), proginfo in every back end (see optimizer thread). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.3 — Done: the back ends link against liblink (f606c1be80) and start emitting code for the new liveness maps (f056daf075); amd64p32 initialisation linkarchinit (e31a1ce109, d4896fb876), register-width stack alignment (3d5e219e02).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: registerize small structs/arrays in 5g and 8g (527ae57e65); explicit zeroing simplified so *x = T{} needs no write barrier (3c40ee0fe0); fatal “out of registers” (c1c5d479bd); 5g does not make register variables for directly called functions (bb4a358af3).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: back ends converted to Go and moved to cmd/internal/gc (8c195bdf12, 3af0d791be); portable cgen/regalloc/componentgen (b115c35ee3, b960263244), reg.c portable (ad88fd1d4a), cmd/gc made a library (349ecfb0d6, eb1774fa19); 9g and 7g added (see port threads); go tool compile/go tool link replace 5g/5l etc. (17eba6e6b7). Left open: machine-translated C idioms (goto, pointer arithmetic) cleaned only gradually (4492811c05, acba34e45f).

Register allocation and the peephole optimizer (reg.c, peep.c)

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: replaced by the SSA register allocator; the old optimizer was gone before go1.17 → continues as Register allocator, scheduler and block-level backend passes (1.18+)

Continues in: Register allocation, flag allocation and stack slots (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. On top of the on-the-fly regalloc, each back end had reg.c (called regopt) and peep.c. regopt builds a flow graph (Flow/Reg) over the Prog list, assigns each local/arg/global a Var (a bit in Bits sets), solves liveness, and “paints” (paint1/paint2) non-address-taken variables into free registers when width, stack offset and etype agree. peep does copy propagation (copyprop/copyu/subprop), redundant-move removal and fixjmp. First cut 2dd16a3208 (2008-11-18) and e081f25c3e; registerization of builtin structures (strings, slices, interfaces) 3dc3ef4cf7, 96cbdd62b6; large functions skipped (bc15b94181).

Correctness drove most of the work: liveness for registers was added to 8g in 2011 by modelling each machine register as a pseudo-variable (84f291b1bd), so a temporary whose range was nested in a live BX span could no longer receive BX; one commit (e419535f2a) repaired a regression that registerized nothing (“2-3x slower”); loop detection was confused by dead code with rpo 0, fixed together with a JMP-to-JMP squashing pass (e2d326b878). In 1.2 the per-opcode switches duplicated across reg.c/peep.c were replaced by proginfo (instruction flags plus registers set/used/indexed): the 6g version (24c8035fbe) found that copyu listed neither INCB, JPS, MOVAPD, MOVBWSX, MOVBWZX, PCDATA, POPQ, PUSHQ, STD, TESTB, TESTQ nor XCHGL and needc only a handful of carry-using instructions; 8g and 5g followed (ac0df6ce89, a07218385c), flow-graph code moved to portable popt (b3b87143f2, dbf96addfb).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: optimizer and indexing/op= improvements (2dd16a3208, e081f25c3e, a6182dab47, 9a5c7eab16, c8a66a98ff); constant propagation for assignments (567a7bf664); 8g optimizer (0eb2a79ff3, 4ab0ce107a); aliasing fixes (bedfc2c2f1, cd00bc78da); ARM optimizer (90ca4d75a4, 4ed17ceace), disabled for the release (1c99bdc8e5, d88f717da6), peep re-enabled (1f55105f66, 2799e0ecb9, dc331e6565, 63c24081a0); register liveness (84f291b1bd); “registerize variables again” (e419535f2a); loop finding (e2d326b878); flush modified globals aggressively (8998835543); constant propagation friendly to inlining (fff732ea2c); byte-move rewrite in 8g with up to -69.83% on crc32 (23f6479be6). Left open: ARM peephole disabled in releases; optimizer bugs recurring.
  • Go 1.1 — Done: 5c regopt re-enabled (70db440885); 6g peephole (3d3b4906f9: shifts do not stop subprop, redundant MOVLQZX removed, early loads); fixjmp for 6c/8c (5cb1ed2189); ONAME nodes recycled to denote registers (45fe306ac8); return registers optimizable (b73a1a8e32, bdd9f29780); 8g drops redundant temporaries before regopt (fa316ba4d8, 14f3276c9d, extended to SSE2 cf77dd37e7: Erf frame 220 → 84 bytes, Lgamma 948 → 44); 5g peephole reactivation incl. EOR → MVN and MOVB elimination (542dd8b9fb, 3f26c5e124); short-integer arithmetic eliminated where possible (8f3c2055bd); componentgen for 5g and for small arrays/structs on 6g (ee3e2ac1a6, 16072c7497, 022b361ae2: the 64-bit int had made it ineffective); 6c rotate/shift peephole (41ec481a53, bb192d1399: (x<<a)|(x>>b) becomes a rotate).
  • Go 1.2 — Done: proginfo in all three (24c8035fbe, ac0df6ce89, a07218385c, 9a0a59f171); portable optimization logic and flow graph (b3b87143f2, dbf96addfb); temporary-merging pass using greedy linear scan (Poletto-Sarkar), cutting the number of functions with too many vars in godoc from 83 to 32 (fa72679f07, 72636eb506); O(n) reset loop removed from copyprop (6d47de2f40); faster compilation by memset (06e686def6); MOVBS/MOVHS pseudo-instructions on ARM to make short-integer semantics explicit (3670337097, 357f733695). Left open: the back ends only track the first 128 variables per function (commit text, fa72679f07).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: no credit for NOPs in allocation (1848d71445); more aliasing by fixing etype mismatches (03c0f3fea9, 0a8a719ded preserve wide values in large functions); globals and results flushed/loaded correctly (f5184d3437); undefined instruction has no successors (85e4cb2f10); liveness-aware regopt fixes (26ad5d4ff0, 684332f47c, 1afbceb599: fat vardef-initialised variables live at calls; up to 7% slower end-to-end).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: register variables for small structs/arrays on 5g/8g (527ae57e65); registerized addr nodes cleared so full registerized temporaries stop reserving stack (be2ad1d7f5); optimizer failure fatal in the C compilers (3147d2c4ee).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: float-constant propagation and MOVSD $0 → XORPS (43c87aa481); 9g regopt (743bdf612a) and peephole (ed5488eece); Bits as uint64 array (fa32e922d5); registerization limits raised (d47fe8092e) and extended to 7g/9g (e040fd4654); cached ProgInfo (fd38dbc8a1); reg.c portable (ad88fd1d4a); debug prints (5b38501a4f). Left open: generated temps in bool codegen (a44becef4a) still produced extra moves.
  • Go 1.6 — Done: register fix for == (6ec1809b83), regopt must not use REGTMP on ppc64 or CX in PIC (0357c38adf, 61da0e92d0, 9514285da9); AVARLIVE in peep for arm/arm64/mips64/ppc64 (5f23bc8903); duffcopy clobbering X0 (ffb20631fc, 0bef88aa5f).

Expression and statement code quality in 6g/8g/5g (division, bounds checks, loops, slices, interfaces)

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: superseded by SSA rules and lowering → continues as amd64 code generation and GOAMD64 microarchitecture levels (1.18+)

Continues in: amd64 and 386 instruction selection (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. A long run of targeted improvements, each tied to a benchmark. Integer division by constants was implemented in 6g in August 2009 (f1baf78247 powers of two; 34f76b5de5 “integer division by a constant done”, with rotate-carry instructions) and in 1.1 moved into the walk pass (4cc9de9147) so 5g and 8g got shifts and magic multiplies; 64-bit division stayed in 6g, and restore magic multiply for /=, %= (061061e77c). Bounds checks: panicindex calls moved out of line so hot loops hold more useful code per cache line (fefae6eed1; two new instruction forms with expected-not-taken branches reversed); loop conditions marked likely so loops are laid out contiguously (001b75c942, replacing expecttaken); conditional branches gbranch take a likely argument. Slicing: x[lo:hi] expanded in the front end (40af78c19e), copy to a direct memmove call with a new OSPTR node for the data pointer (ff416a3f19), convT2E inlined for uintptr-shaped T (8f84328fdc).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: divide-by-constant (f1baf78247, 34f76b5de5), 8-bit div/mod (3f91f80a21), inline slicearray/sliceslice (9bf597a210, bf0130cc0f), x[lo:] (652f55672d), scaled indexing (c8a66a98ff), 64-bit shift fix (e5bd12ea90), NaN-safe comparisons (109a976355, ef46a9ddac), avoid unneeded conversions in bounds checks (d14baee96e), a[byte(x)] truncation (ba50599e46), bounds checks off support (c332ff42fe), 8g: float->uint64 (a551ffe809, f570d9d765).
  • Go 1.1 — Done: out-of-line panicindex (fefae6eed1), contiguous loops (001b75c942), rotate code (c6ce44822c, later partly rolled back for 8g 251199c430), float->uint64 truncation fix (e80f6a4de1), inline slice[arr,str] (40af78c19e), convT2E (8f84328fdc), nil-comparison without extra agen (ff642e290f), no LEA of interfaces on method calls (b45b6fd1c7), 6g float move without MOVSD between registers (a768de8347), sbop swap logic (de96df1b02), simplified integer division (a617d06252), zerostack experiment: user-visible GOEXPERIMENT=zerostack clears the stack on function entry to avoid GC false positives (b7603cfc2c); cmd/gc: avoid duplicate allocation during inlining (a72f9f46a2); large-model flag for 6c/6g (fe14ee52cc); more nil-pointer-to-large-struct checks (578dc3a96c). Left open: zerostack was expensive (the commit says so) and opt-in.
  • Go 1.2 — Done: copy inlined as memmove (ff416a3f19), nil-check on &x and removal of redundant &x.Field checks (999a36f9af, aa0439ba65), 6c/8c avoid long multiplication (2c0b00744f), full 64-bit address in block copy (f268c295a3), very wide offsets (9c21ce54dd), no constant propagation of non-constant LEA (3c3ce8e7fb), clearfat de-interleaved (85a7c090c4), defer caller line numbers via a real NOP (7e97d39879; XCHG AX,AX / AND.EQ R0,R0,R0).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: 6g inline copies of up to 4 words, after reflect.Value grew to 4 words and json fell ~50% (to ~5%) (0ea20bc981); unaligned load/stores for trailing bytes in sgen/clearfat (2b93c4dd06); small zeroings in straight-line code (14664050b9); bypass DATA for integer-constant data (4acb70d377); a register for nil-checking constants (52e6d7c622).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: explicit zeroing without write barrier, MOVs instead of repeated STOSQ (3c40ee0fe0); extern = <N> code (0edafefc36); no address-as-constant in amd64 instructions (ce35994d4e).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: float-constant propagation (43c87aa481), componentgen on string constants (94410c794e), zero via register (01ef6dbfa5, 8f734d4e2f), 2- and 3-word sgen (747c849833, c1c3ce6b36), boolean values via SETcc instead of jumps (13cb62c764), hardware math.Sqrt on amd64/arm (92dba0d278), runtime.getg inlined (92c826b1b2, garbage benchmark +2.6%), MOV instead of LEA 0(R0) (0f0bc0f016), shifts for power-of-two indexing (135389d0ff), write-barrier-aware slice update x = x[:i] (d447279927) and typedmemmove from sgen (2a73559023, 2b7505e28a for RISC), panicindex marked as not returning (fc595b78d2), ginscmp hook (f8d14fc3a0), generated temps in bool codegen (a44becef4a), missing write barrier in append(x, BigStructWithPointers) (366ba526e8, 9c9e36b340).
  • Go 1.6 — Done: test-first-field-of-struct special case for amd64 and 386 (9aed0b7e3d, f3b064ae01), magic-multiply no longer smashes AX (03c8164849), write barrier on type switch (e3033fc535), Syscall-like functions for liveness (1ac637c766), args_stackmap not for func _ (292ad59291).

Stack frames, pointer maps and liveness analysis in the compiler

Span: Go 1.2 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: liveness analysis (plive) and per-call-site stack maps remain; pointer bitmaps are still 1 bit per word → continues as Stack slot merging, liveness and stack maps (1.18+)

Continues in: Liveness, stack maps, safepoints and write barriers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Precise stack scanning needed, for every call site, a map of which frame slots hold live pointers. Go 1.2 built the plumbing: the C compiler emits argument pointer maps (9b1f1833de) and locals bitmaps (73c93a404c); a dedicated FUNCDATA number carries the runtime’s GC metadata, and the old pseudo-instructions and linker code that handled them are removed (48769bf546); the assemblers learn PCDATA/FUNCDATA (47b89a37d9, 8c741c97f7); cmd/cc records the size of locals (e4b5cbde46) and the argument size for every call (4e141145b7, 7b3c8b7ac8); interface and eface words are encoded distinctly in the map (abc516e420) so the collector can use the type word to decide whether the data word is a pointer (21ea5103a4). Because the maps could still see stale slots, pointers in the frame and the results are zeroed on entry (7910cd68b5, “up to 30% slowdown”, an “intermediate step”), with “has pointers” separated from “needs zeroing” (3b4d792606).

Go 1.3 computed the maps by dataflow liveness (f056daf075): a backward analysis over the flow graph yields, at each safepoint, the set of live pointer-bearing slots (“mean reduction of 65% in the number of stack slots scanned” under GOGC=1 all.bash), but the commit notes scanning was still not precise because pointers confound reaching definitions. Variables are tracked as whole units; compiler-inserted VARDEF marks the start of life for fat variables, placed “before the initialization but after any final use” (7a7c0ffb47), and VARKILL ends the life of temporaries whose address went to runtime map/chan calls (b700cb4974). Variables that are “ambiguously live” (live on some paths, uninitialised on others) are zeroed on entry; only those are zeroed after 6722d45631 rather than all pointer-bearing locals, with address-taken-but-non-escaping variables handled in ca9975a45e. In 1.4 assembly functions get maps derived from their Go prototypes (myfunc.args_stackmap, 99f7df0598), slices and strings are treated like pointers (613383c765), and argsize PCDATA is no longer generated (68c1c6afa0). In 1.5 the stack, data and bss maps shrink to 1 bit per word because there are no multiword GC types left (4d0f3a1c95).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.2 — Done: funcdata/pcdata plumbing (48769bf546, 47b89a37d9, 8c741c97f7, de6da4a8bd), C and Go argument/locals bitmaps (9b1f1833de, 73c93a404c, 2db5e4bb0b), interface encoding (abc516e420, 21ea5103a4), zero pointers on entry (7910cd68b5, 3b4d792606, d3b04f46b5, 390656affd), nosplit pointer maps from the linker (037a1a9f31), . Left open: maps conservative; liveness analysis not written (commit text: “intermediate step”).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: liveness-based maps (f056daf075; d4f68f2892, 6965a752a7, bc9691c465 dead-value maps disabled/renamed), compile-time speedups (0e97f4187e: up to 7x, 145edc283f), many correctness fixes: addressed results 824e918ca4, block-move init 91b1f7cb15, tail-jump wrappers 02ae91f342, funcs ending in panic ab9e8d068a, non-returning functions af545660d5, fat variables 7a7c0ffb47, no fallthrough edge after panic 28479f2c32, zeroing to enable precise stack accounting a81692e265 (only effective with a debug flag), zero only ambiguously live variables 6722d45631, 1ca1cbea65, VARKILL for runtime-call temporaries b700cb4974, stack map entries redone to avoid false retention 1b45cc45e3, don’t zero more than needed 47acf16709, relaxed zeroing in 6g f400d9aafc, input variables vs regopt 26ad5d4ff0, globals/args/results f5184d3437, vardef-initialised fat variables live at calls 1afbceb599 (slowdown up to 7%), reflect.callXX maps cee8bcabfa. Left open: zeroing “pretty inefficient” (issue 7624) and too many ambiguously live variables (issue 7345).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: local type information is emitted explicitly (see the 1.1 note on 1d5dc4fd481.1, 43c04ba1b81.1, aa3efb28f01.1); args_stackmap for assembly functions from Go prototypes (99f7df0598), slices/strings scanned like pointers (613383c765), all G frames copyable (00365b13b4), argsize PCDATA dropped (68c1c6afa0), auxiliary symbols marked pointer-free (8b20e7bb7e), runtime package decls never heap-promoted (064acace5b), liveness ~10x faster (7aa3031eba), invalid GC pointer crashes (11e53e46a6), emit code for extern init (0edafefc36).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: 1-bit stack/data/bss bitmaps (4d0f3a1c95), fixed-size frames in goproc/deferproc (53c5226f9f), larger stack guard for unoptimized builds (a55b131393), liveness debugging (fa7efa2cb0), gc: restore stack frame debugging (aed88be021). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.6 — Done: Syscall-like assembly functions recognised for liveness so arguments stay live for the whole call (1ac637c766); no args_stackmap for func _ (292ad59291); AVARLIVE in peephole passes (5f23bc8903).

Stack frame layout, prologues, stack split and frame pointers

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: prologue generation per architecture in cmd/internal/obj/*; frame pointers kept on amd64 (default) and arm64 → continues as Prologue, frame pointer, stack split and function alignment (cmd/internal/obj) (1.18+)

Continues in: Prologues, frame pointers, NOFRAME and tail calls (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • motivating issue #10587 cmd/gc: stack split check does not follow static branch prediction rules of modern CPUs referenced by 3 of this thread's commits
  • discussion get rid of stack check prolog golang-nuts · linked from #10587

Design. Segmented-stack prologues are emitted by the assembler/linker pass (originally in the linkers, from 1.3 in liblink and then cmd/internal/obj/<arch>/obj*.go): compare SP (or SP minus frame) with g->stackguard and call runtime.morestack, with the frame and argument sizes passed via a magic $a-b operand (3f982aeaf6, 2008). The compilers lay out locals: 2011 saw compaction by sharing slots (2ac375b2df, ARM 2ad42a8249) and a unified layout (5ddf6255a1); 6c/8c frames were cut about in half in 1.1 (139448fe95). In 1.5, with the ARM and arm64 and x86 prologues, “static branch prediction guesses forward branches aren’t taken”, so the forward branch now means “grow” (f4b48de3ad x86, 54789eff38 arm64) and ARM executes one conditional branch rather than three conditional instructions, adding 4 bytes per function (5353cde080). Knowledge of the fixed part of the stack frame was centralised (97055dc1f1) because ppc64le shared libraries need the TOC pointer at 24(R1); larger frames raised the nosplit limit (c1b6e392f5).

The framepointer GOEXPERIMENT (1.5) makes the amd64 toolchain keep BP chains like gcc -fno-omit-frame-pointer so Linux perf/VTune can unwind Go stacks: compilers don’t clobber BP and liblink emits the saving prologue (3c0fee10db); duffcopy/duffzero are fixed for it (08af4c3a79).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: morestack magic operand (3f982aeaf6), stack-split segment size bug (cb15bbe748), argsize rounding smash on 32-bit (de663b2d6b), 5l morestack for ARM (1ac2cfc720), NOSPLIT checks in cc (36c5c5bf40), frame compaction (2ac375b2df, 2ad42a8249, 5ddf6255a1), .
  • Go 1.1 — Done: 6c/8c stack frames cut by about half (139448fe95), clearstk deleted (96b0594833), fix for large stacks (d127ed5378).
  • Go 1.2 — Done: pointer-map-aware zeroing of frames and stkptrsize (d3b04f46b5, 390656affd).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: register-width stack alignment for amd64p32 (3d5e219e02), zero at start of frame more efficiently (383963b506), NaCl zeroing (bfbb2e827b).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: ARM wrapper prologue (fb818eab7f).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: frame pointer experiment (3c0fee10db, 08af4c3a79, 90c0fefe51), predictable prologues (f4b48de3ad, 5353cde080, 54789eff38), correct pc/sp info for the prologue (0a3c991fd3), arm64 frame alignment (3952057cf6, 034a10d44c), stack guard (a55b131393), Link.Symmorestack removed (4b23b50fb4), 386 prologue fixes in position-independent mode.

Zeroing and copying: Duff’s device, REP, unaligned moves and AVX2 runtime assembly

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: duffzero/duffcopy still used by amd64 at go1.17 → continues as Duff’s device replaced by generated loops; Zero/Move lowering (1.20+)

Continues in: Memory clearing and copying: Zero, Move and Duff’s device (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Compiler-generated copies and clears (sgen, clearfat) went from REP MOVSQ/STOSQ to straight-line code and Duff’s device. In 1.0 the convention was that the direction flag is always clear (8f53bc0612) so the compiler could emit memcpy/memset as REP. In 1.3, since REP has “really high startup overhead”, 6g inlines copies up to four words (0ea20bc981, after reflect.Value grew to 4 words and json went ~50% slower), uses overlapping unaligned loads/stores for trailing bytes (2b93c4dd06), zeroes small objects in straight-line code (14664050b9), and the runtime uses a Duff’s device instead of REP (6c7cbf086c, 51b72d94de, 383963b506). In 1.4 repeated STOSQ became MOVs (3c40ee0fe0). In 1.5 2- and 3-word sgen were special-cased because they are 85% (6g) / 70% (8g) of sgen calls (747c849833), and duffzero used MOVUPS to zero 16 bytes at a time (2421c6e3df). Duff’s device is disabled on NaCl (c6a41a3559) and on Plan 9 for duffcopy (50ad337238) and ppc64 duffzero (cda1fc0071).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: direction-bit convention (8f53bc0612), fat copy overlap (30fd44cf9d), reverse character copy in sgen (1d0b65d33f).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: the changes listed above (0ea20bc981, 2b93c4dd06, 14664050b9, 6c7cbf086c, 51b72d94de, 383963b506); Duff off on NaCl (c6a41a3559). Left open: “TODO: REP still used for reverse copying when regions overlap”.
  • Go 1.4 — Done: 3c40ee0fe0;
  • Go 1.5 — Done: 747c849833, c1c3ce6b36, 01ef6dbfa5, 8f734d4e2f (zero via a register in componentgen), faster aeshash hashing several streams in parallel (7a4a64e8f3).
  • Go 1.6 — Done: MOVUPS-based duffzero (2421c6e3df), AVX2 versions of Compare, string compare, IndexByte and memclr (0e23ca41d9, 967564be7e, 321a40721b up to -49% at 4K, b597e1ed54), SSE4.1 Floor/Ceil (37cfb2e07e, ~-30%), duffcopy clobbers X0 (ffb20631fc, 0bef88aa5f).

liblink: a shared assembler/linker library

Span: Go 1.3 → Go 1.5 · Status at go1.17: converted to Go as cmd/internal/obj in 1.5 (this thread); the C library itself was deleted (3317e7f19a) → continues as Prologue, frame pointer, stack split and function alignment (cmd/internal/obj) (1.18+)

Continues in: cmd/internal/obj: Prog/LSym refactoring, concurrent backend and object-writing (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc Go 1.3 Linker Overhaul cited in this thread's commits

Design. For the Go 1.3 linker plan, the per-architecture logic that lived in 5l/6l/8l (instruction selection, span layout, prologue/stack-split rewriting, TLS and branch fix-ups) was extracted into src/liblink, linked into compilers (5g/6g/8g), C compilers (5c/6c/8c) and assemblers (5a/6a/8a) (f7aaa553da, 76a8c873cf, f606c1be80; the C-compiler change also updated cc/gc: 870e821ded). The big commit a9f6db58ce (“move instruction selection + layout into compilers, assemblers”) added a new object file reader/writer (liblink/objfile.c), a pcdata iterator, removed the “line number stack” and “path fragments” from object files and the linker, made DWARF a single compilation unit, and disabled the check for chains of nosplit functions (issue 6931). The point is that each tool emits finished machine code and the linker only relocates and lays out symbols. Object files gained a version number so later format changes are easy (0e8de61d73, “changes we know we want to make, but not before Go 1.3”), the arch-specific constants were removed from the format (8d39e55c65), and a leaf bit so the linker records correct frame sizes (needed for ARM tracebacks, cc08d9232c). A direct consequence: liblink can no longer depend on link-time decisions. linkmode was removed from the ARM (dab127baf5) and x86 paths, which broke cgo TLS on ARM until b377c9c6a9 and 1dd4da1459 (adding an AMRC instruction for MRC/MCR so rewriting no longer matches bit patterns of AWORD).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.3 — Done: adoption by assemblers, C compilers and Go compilers (f7aaa553da, 76a8c873cf, f606c1be80), new object format (a9f6db58ce), many Plan 9 / warning fixes (b9bed39714, 52ee63f544, 6e97513012, 0830f64bf0), explicit field for duplicate globl detection (4890502af6), either of conflicting symbols may say dupok (c9f12d2289), symgrow check (6111dc4e71), TLS register on 386/amd64 so 4(GS) rewrites are explicit (90093f0634; the commit says rewrites “had gotten out of control”), linkmode removal and ARM cgo fixes (dab127baf5, b377c9c6a9, 1dd4da1459, 9ed5995cfe), object version (0e8de61d73), leaf bit (cc08d9232c), NaCl morestack (9460cf7825, 88f84b3e41), field tracking (d9c9665f1d), remove never-executed code (f4ecfaa442). Left open: nosplit-chain check disabled (issue 6931).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: preliminary plan9/amd64 (decd810945), nacl/arm (783bcba84d), LinkArch.textflag() instead of thechar switches (3c24b60fd3), big-endian support (08ee2661f2), shorter zeroing-register encoding (24db881689), MOVBQZX as MOVZBL (bbc6bb9a99), literal-word comparison on ARM (b916dc1992), way to avoid pc-relative addressing for Solaris (4516a60062), DATA must be offset-ordered with no overlap (5e6bd29c2c), %^ verb and C_* constants moved (d69d0fe92b), arm MRC replacement generated in liblink (0b36211cfb), gotos rewritten for translation (8e0e09ae7d), fb818eab7f, 20a5de9eb6, a6feaf3aff, ae027f52fe.
  • Go 1.5 — Done: the C library is converted to Go (see C→Go thread), made uniform (see cmd/internal/obj thread) and finally deleted (3317e7f19a); liblink fixes during the transition (0185ba76ed, e04c8b063f do not patch jumps to jumps to symbols, 3be0a0ef6f, 52d277906d, dba9eb3369 GOEXPERIMENT in runtime and liblink, 281ae92881 SETcc encoding, ab9ec2e401, 6c78443b3e code for debugging bad returns, 9b1b0a46dd fail for too-large register offset).

Normalising Prog/Addr in cmd/internal/obj (the portable instruction representation)

Span: Go 1.5 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: the design (portable Prog, Addr with TYPE_*, From3/RegTo2, shared A* numbers, Link context) is still in place → continues as Prologue, frame pointer, stack split and function alignment (cmd/internal/obj) (1.18+)

Continues in: cmd/internal/obj: Prog/LSym refactoring, concurrent backend and object-writing (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Before 1.5, each liblink architecture had its own Prog/Addr conventions. In January 2015 Russ Cox made them uniform so that one set of architecture-independent passes (and cmd/asm) could operate on them: the zero Prog is valid and has as set to AXXX instead of AGOK (76fed5426c); common instructions get fixed numbers ANOP, ATEXT, AGLOBL, ACALL, AJMP, ARET with arm/ppc64 aliases (2e5b065ac2); TEXT $frame-arg is encoded the same way on all architectures (72521319c7); TEXT/GLOBL flags live in p->from3 (77a415e5a6) and DATA size in from3.offset (3ac37c72ae); constants must use TYPE_ADDR not TYPE_CONST, with an input checker in liblink/pass.c (1f2d7bf44f); ARM conditions renumbered so C_SCOND_NONE == 0 (e66ad16ddb); dead p->back computation removed (6654188190). The portable Prog/Addr layer was ported to every back end in five parallel commits (5a2771e286, 0d599909e9, 604138e87b, a5b1baeed7, da47902d02). Later cleanups: Addr.U struct replaced by Val interface{} (532ccae154), Prog.From3 a pointer (c413c45e6d), two unused fields removed (2286e452bd, 1378173785, 4ed7d06a87), Pcrel and Comefrom combined (c04813e130), global Aconv/Dconv/Rconv and Prog.String replacing per-arch Pconv (74e88dfdee, 29421cbb5b, daddeb2686, 24a43e6a75, 40ff393e4c), go generated Anames (4b981ed3e6), unary-destination tables moved from asm into obj (8974fb9ba5), symbol table as a map (049eee6806), line history reimplemented with O(log n) lookup (861546543a), Ctxt.Endian deleted (ea7be5170a), Link.Tlsoffset removed (7bf959c67a), ProgInfo layout (b795ce9ab0, 30b966307f), keyed ProgInfo literals (2468227038).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.5 — Done: the list above; cmd/internal/obj created from liblink (d6f6e420fc, 24dfaba6d1, 1fc330d8fe, dc7b54bed2), shift of x86 SHRQ second source to From3 (3d0397a4f4), CALL *name(SB) (b66a509992), PINSRD (29f18f2800), CMPPS memory third arg (59584ede73), cleanup (ad49c7bb62, fc28fd1eb8, e7ffafdb6e, 0088ddc3a0, 873483c682, 8d16253c90). Left open: the code generator still produced Prog lists per function and wrote objects at the end.
  • Go 1.6 — Done: code layout (span) separated from object writing so the compiler could lay out each function as it is compiled, “should reduce the working set of the compiler. But not until Go 1.7” (ed03dab853); Tlsoffset removal (7bf959c67a); ProgInfo layout (b795ce9ab0).

The Plan 9 C compilers (cc, 5c/6c/8c) in the Go toolchain

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.5 · Status at go1.17: removed in 1.5 (4a42fae2cd on dev.cc); runtime was rewritten in Go and assembly

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc Go 1.3+ Compiler Overhaul listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc dev.cc branch plan listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc Go 1.5 Bootstrap Plan listed in Go: A Documentary

Design. src/cmd/cc plus 5c/6c/8c compiled the runtime’s C code and cgo helpers; the tree adopted Plan 9’s lib9/libbio in 2008 (69b74c3953) and brought in 8c/8l/8a (4dee747fb9, af0143ce03) and 5a/5c/5l (db3a21d7c6) from the Inferno distribution. The compilers shared cc/pgen.c/pswt.c (27432d67ec) and their own register allocator (reg.c) and peephole (peep.c), with alignment rules kept consistent with the matching Go back ends (7fbf9fcba9, b331f3cfd0). Go-specific extensions: #pragma textflag, dataflag, dynexport, varargck countpos/type for the Windows stdcall helpers (fe2ccb53c0), NOPTRBSS (5bcad92f07), 21-bit rune wide strings (781b2a2519), PREFETCH builtin (d42495aa80, ARM 278d4a583d), nested package calls like sync»atomic·LoadInt32 (8be5e8a419), and a mode that emits Go definitions of C types and variables (efda876a94) used to generate defs_*.go; in 1.4 Eface maps to interface{} (948bb9150e) and structs without tags are disallowed (3ffd29fb2c). For precise GC cc emits argument pointer maps and locals bitmaps (9b1f1833de, 73c93a404c), gc bitmaps in read-only memory (a26c01ad44) and gains the same linkarchinit as gc for amd64p32 (d4896fb876). Optimizations in 6c: avoid long multiplication (2c0b00744f), rotates (bb192d1399, 41ec481a53), NaN-safe floating point (109a976355), fixjmp in regopt (5cb1ed2189), 64-bit switch values (6481e37d28, d89b7173c2).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: the imports and 8c/5c bring-up above; many 6c/8c code-gen fixes (902a4d5f29 large constants, 5e5476c2fe byte* difference, d4ad8e8ce3 misaligned arguments, 494bcc80e4 extern static registers in 5c, ee7c64efe5 extern register vars only in MOVL, 3e0adc9ffb vlong condition, 5124e66fca), removal of fixed-size buffers (139a053733, 77053797e0, 0e47c75f60), -S line numbers (2cda191aef), 5c do not use R9/R10 (c475c3071a) and gcc/Plan 9 build fixes (b0449c50f7, 5ea4d73b17, 4c6280b0f1, 3f2cc8ba7e, c8c6e1961d), b0449c50f7.
  • Go 1.1 — Done: GOROOT_FINAL (bcdafaa582), 6c rotates (bb192d1399, 41ec481a53), MOVQL for explicit truncation (e530d6a1e0), 5c regopt re-enabled (70db440885), R12 and F8–F15 usable on ARM (d87bc2f0c0), uint right-shift constant eval (34ad3995e0), large model flag (fe14ee52cc), dynamic-linker autodetection (dac4c3eee9), struct literal side effects (c13866db7f).
  • Go 1.2 — Done: cc rejects unions with pointers (dbee8ad0f9), isolated textflag/dataflag (2449909d81), wide-char fix (5b15b44434), full 64-bit block copy (f268c295a3), pointer maps (9b1f1833de, 2db5e4bb0b), %Q (237e7c134c), AFUNCDATA PC fix (de6da4a8bd), fix undefined behaviour (8d5ec52e6c).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: liblink (76a8c873cf), NaCl (7954b2b90b), amd64p32 (d4896fb876), bitmaps in rodata (a26c01ad44).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: Eface → interface{} (948bb9150e), no tag-less structs (3ffd29fb2c), make optimizer failure fatal (3147d2c4ee), diagnose Go calling C (0bb14d74f1), stop emitting argsize PCDATA (68c1c6afa0), #pragma pack off error (86c4c4f00c). Left open: the runtime still contained C (c2go translation was the plan).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: cc, 5c, 6c, 8c removed on dev.cc (4a42fae2cd), 9c removed (1a68ac2538, an earlier 9c existed on dev.power64: 83f6aadf16, 95e8a3a1da, 860f941e7f, 25bde37af4), lexbody/macbody deleted after the assemblers were replaced (184eb0ac9e).

Assemblers: 5a/6a/8a/9a and the Go cmd/asm

Span: Go 1.0 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: cmd/asm (cmd/asm/internal/{arch,asm,flags,lex} + cmd/internal/obj) is the assembler → continues as arm64 code generation and assembler (and the other per-arch assembler threads) (1.18+)

Continues in: x86 assembler: AVX, AVX2, AVX-512 and the instruction table (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · ARM64 assembler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · 32-bit ARM, MIPS and PPC64 assemblers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • talk The Design of the Go Assembler. GopherCon 2016. Aug 18, 2016. listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc Go 1.3 Linker Overhaul cited in this thread's commits

Design. The Plan 9-derived assemblers were yacc programs (a.y, lex.c) per architecture. They gained x86 coverage over time (386 SSE2 5da37c0901, XMM registers 755e13877f, AES 297bb12809, CMPPD e5009e29ea, IMULL grammar 1738dc0e71, $(-1) forms 6d9c02aea3, MOVQL ea86752206, amd64p32 e509bbc943, SETPC a6feaf3aff), ARM (PLD 2031252fb8, MULW{T,B} a0084b3494, m/g registers 5d081792b6) and pseudo-ops (PCDATA 47b89a37d9, FUNCDATA 8c741c97f7). In 1.3 they used liblink (f7aaa553da) and in late 2014 labels became function-scoped (b55791e200).

For Go 1.5 cmd/asm replaced them. Rob Pike’s design (dev.cc): a single assembler driven by cmd/asm/internal/arch tables (register names, instruction aliases, per-arch operand rules), lex (a macro-processing tokenizer with #define, #ifdef, #include; d6eb21e331 rewrote the macro processor), asm (parser and instruction builder), flags, producing obj.Prog lists consumed by cmd/internal/obj. Development was bootstrapped by converting the old assemblers mechanically to Go (9e2f8fdb6f, 4ca2fc4d8b “new5a etc, cmd/internal/asm”) and verifying the new assembler byte-for-byte against them: cmd/asm was first the “verify” pass in cmd/go (“verifyAsm”), then made the first assembler (4100f7d95c), and the runtime was the last package verified (e59ed477c3). Once identical, the C assemblers and cmd/internal/asm were deleted (3af0d791be, ba0c142d32, 861af80458).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.0 — Done: documentation of the assemblers and loaders (b5ab5d4f12), Windows paths (aed2c06dcb), fixed buffers (07d3e0dce4, 0e47c75f60, 77053797e0), delete 8a’s dreg l.s (783c46b197).
  • Go 1.1 — Done: PLD (2031252fb8), MULW (a0084b3494), SSE2 and XMM (5da37c0901, 755e13877f), AES (297bb12809), GOROOT_FINAL (6af069f3e1), delete dead code (6a22e2fb3f).
  • Go 1.2 — Done: flag parsing (8124a02cb2), PCDATA/FUNCDATA (47b89a37d9, 8c741c97f7), m/g for ARM (5d081792b6), MOVBS/MOVHS (3670337097).
  • Go 1.3 — Done: liblink (f7aaa553da), generated .y fixes (426b48a775), MOVQL (ea86752206), amd64p32 (e509bbc943), link to the new assembler document (0bdd90bc0a).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: AJxx condition-code docs (c6442c994a), SETPC encoding (a6feaf3aff).
  • Go 1.5 — Done: the new assembler: arch, addr and lex packages and the assembler proper (6017f68029, 40eb0ed0d8, 8642639575, fdeee3a538), identical output to new6a (89162307cd), TEXT $3-2 parsing (92e5120c77), macros (d6eb21e331, 5beec6a699), rewrite for the new obj API (cb19a20121), runtime final fixes (e59ed477c3), architectures: 386 (ef664199cb), ARM (c497349a5b, 5d111b898a, 5d987f1513 MCR), ppc64 (e559c5cce2, 5b9429d122, adff896e4c), ppc64le (9c0c050773), arm64 (18d9ddc35c, a175fa3bc3, ef49b4ca78); 4(SP) illegal except on 386 (345350bf07); LOOP as a branch on x86 (9a420f4cf3); order of assemblers (4100f7d95c); removing the objects when assembly fails (3b1d0d0f07); function-scoped labels (b55791e200, b528063099); old assemblers deleted (621d75999f rename to old5a, ba0c142d32, 861af80458). Left open: shift handling and macros had follow-up bugs (58d177c63e, 989b372a5c, d6eb21e331).
  • Go 1.6 — Done: robustness against fuzzing (7437e3f02e, df37c4b987, 63e2bed0ab, 5e89acb580, 980cb0caf2, 173bf3487f, 49580db149, 49065cbfe4), nested #if (eaea5ade2b), more than one encoding error reported (36edf48a10), -e flag (02717bdc20), mips64 (43ea305435), ARM CMPF/CMPD (36af087aef), arm64 condition-code aliases (61a3ebed55); x86: YMM registers (d2b0c387b2), VEX encodings VZEROUPPER, VMOVDQU, VMOVDQA, VMOVNTDQ (9dd81d6227), then “correct, complete” AVX (8d881b811d), BMI-style PDEP/PEXT (0bae38e094), POPCNT (d3ff40fb1f, 7f620a57d0), HADDPD/HADDPS (e634765941), requested amd64 instructions (863d9b66f8), TSX (e9081b3c76), PSRLW fix (d96b4c494f), reject foo(SB)(AX) (9d6427d899).

C→Go translation of the toolchain (liblink, assemblers, compilers; dev.cc)

Span: Go 1.4 → Go 1.5 · Status at go1.17: complete; all tools are Go

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc dev.cc branch plan listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc Go 1.3+ Compiler Overhaul listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc Go 1.5 Bootstrap Plan listed in Go: A Documentary
  • talk The move from C to Go in the toolchain. GopherFest 2015. Jun 10, 2015. listed in Go: A Documentary
  • design doc Go 1.3 Linker Overhaul listed in Go: A Documentary

Design. The dev.cc branch used Russ Cox’s rsc.io/c2go translator to convert the C toolchain mechanically, then hand-fixed leftovers. Preparation (1.4) was annotation-driven: #define to enum, /*c2go */ comments giving the effect of macros, braces in struct initialisers (ebce79446d). Conversion order: first liblink as cmd/internal/obj with a temporary dual mode where C liblink calls go tool objwriter to write objects, selected by $GOOBJ and $GOOBJWRITER and verified against the C output (be818361b9, 725e3a7afb, 283b23297a, d6f6e420fc, 24dfaba6d1, 1fc330d8fe, 2ecefd41fa disabled the GOOBJ=2 default, 25c140aaa0 turned off the verification), then the assemblers (9e2f8fdb6f, 4ca2fc4d8b, 67e7ded029), then the compilers and linkers into cmd/internal/gc, cmd/internal/ld, cmd/new6g etc (8c195bdf12: 88448 lines added). Repeated reconversions (dc7b54bed2, f6791da7ad, 53d4123fbc adding profiling) followed C-side changes until the freeze, when the C implementations were replaced by the Go ones (3af0d791be: 170 files, +9484/-93906) and then the C libraries and their dist code were deleted (3317e7f19a). Source simplifications for translation went into mainline: cmd/gc as a real library (349ecfb0d6), simplifying code (e82003e750, 5c87cf7608, 2286989912, 3be0a0ef6f), and removal of C tricks (subclassing in popt.c 1250d2e374, pointer arithmetic acba34e45f, qsort order 90965718a8). After the switch the Go source was cleaned: goto removal (4492811c05), idiomatic bool fields (25da594c6a, 38a61ff41f, 75883bae28), unembedding Node.Func/Name (3ed9e4ca3c, 8fa14ea8b4), Fprintf-style cleanups (494e317fbf), destuttering (ce469fadd8).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.4 — Done: c2go annotations (ebce79446d). Left open: the actual conversion.
  • Go 1.5 — Done: conversions and the switch (above), go tool compile / go tool link (17eba6e6b7), old assemblers deleted (ba0c142d32), cmd/dist Go constant for external linking (7934199877). Left open: generated code still C-flavoured (acba34e45f).
  • Go 1.6 — Done: janitoring of map/slice literals and gc (3c37a61455, 7d48573d46, 90f69259ec, 932c1e3dd3, dd42eff8fe, 3e476827a6, 6d0178359f, ea4e321d4d).

The ppc64 / ppc64le port (dev.power64, 9g/9a/9l)

Span: Go 1.5 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: production port with shared-library support → continues as PPC64 / Power10 backend (GOPPC64, prefixed instructions, PC-relative code) (1.18+)

Continues in: 32-bit ARM, MIPS and PPC64 assemblers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Multi-architecture SSA ports: PPC64, MIPS64, MIPS32, s390x (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. The port started on 2014-08-06 by importing the Vita Nuova 9a/9c/9l code without modification, “concatenating several cmd/9l files together to form the liblink files” (117b1d4685), then converting 9c/9a to liblink with Go argument passing and both endiannesses (83f6aadf16, bcf7f61f83, 4be75c8f26) and writing 9g from the 6g/5g model (“first check point” 4928b2074b). The code generator copies the template: zerorange (b1c9a8bce3), loops for memmove in sgen (372b5cebe7), ginscon2 for CMP/CMPU (893f28ca16), NaN-correct float compares (27e657ef68, aa739b8d03), MOVD $con(Ra), Rb → ADD (f375c0eb0d), large constants (ba9a11e557), stack split and long conditional branches in liblink (f4529adabe). Bits became a uint64 array (fa32e922d5); progtable gets CC/V/VCC variants (e78777ebfe) and proginfo for DUFFZERO/DUFFCOPY (ee853dacf5, 60f66aa817); regopt (743bdf612a) and a peephole (ed5488eece) were implemented, R_CALLPOWER like ELF R_PPC64_REL24 (6f755f2f8f), R13 avoided (bbd2127909). Frame alignment: 8-byte argument size on power64 (93341e8664, bc8d35a9cf). ARETURN was unified with obj.ARET (9389a86b01, 16310571d1) and ppc64 DS-form loads/stores handled in obj and the linker (5e1d0fcbed).

Go 1.6 added position-independent code: -shared/-dynlink on ppc64 (c23c8d58d6), a TOC pointer maintained in R2 following the ELFv2 ABI: global entry point instructions, local-entry metadata for the system linker, save/restore around calls (368d548417), TOC-relative loads of static data (bd329d47d9), GOT access (2ac993107f), IE-model TLS (a35c85c0cc, further “like a platform linker” c9b8cab16c), no PLT call to morestack (64fbca41c8), stack barriers in ppc64le shared libs (3a1bed82a6), larger minimum frame (97055dc1f1, c1b6e392f5). Regopt must not use REGTMP (0357c38adf).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.5 — Done: the port as above, plus cmd/asm support (e559c5cce2, 9c0c050773), 9g: fix nilopt (810019286f), fix under-zeroing in clearfat (6e86003651), fix addr width and enable MOV* width check (22c929f538, c1e8c57c3d), nilopt (5e4989cf0a disables, 810019286f fixes), REGZERO for the zero register (1e1c9dc2c8). Left open: “disable stack split for now” at the start (05d670f757), “No peep optimizer” on 7g; nilopt disabled initially (5e4989cf0a); suboptimal copy code noted (36f879780a).
  • Go 1.6 — Done: the PIC/TOC work listed above, SRADCC immediate assembly (10c0753761), epilogue for non-leaf generated methods (710b9ad617), archreloc simplification (d821ae2a9e).

The arm64 (ARMv8) port (7g/7a/7l)

Span: Go 1.5 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: production port → continues as arm64 code generation and assembler (1.18+)

Continues in: ARM64 assembler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Multi-architecture SSA ports: ARM, 386, ARM64 (dev.ssa) (Go 1.7 → Go 1.8)

Design. Aram Hăvărneanu’s port landed in March 2015 as three parts: the assembler/obj package (26bbe7ac9b: 32 64-bit integer registers, 32 128-bit vector registers (unused), R31 is either hardware stack pointer RSP or zero register ZR depending on the instruction; hardware SP must be 16-byte aligned), cmd/asm support (18d9ddc35c) and the 7g compiler “based on 9g” (02c1a9d87d, “No peep optimizer yet”). Because ARM64 has no absolute addressing for text, 6e3a2a3f9f removed it from .text; ef49b4ca78 added CSEL; a175fa3bc3 parses register pairs for LDP/STP; 888d44d3c1 uses the zero register in componentgen; e040fd4654 raised registerization; prologues were made predictable (54789eff38); frames must be aligned (3952057cf6) and misaligned frames are rejected except empty ones (034a10d44c); 0f27b91522 introduces RegTo2 instead of a full Addr; 467a2cb73c drops the Reginuse check in clearfat. In 1.6: loads from memory use two instructions rather than three (3a9bc571b0), TLS (72180c3b82 “native-ish”, 80d9106487 initial-exec), GOT access in -dynlink (3534e2bef4), branch enlargement (2a031e6a2a, literal pool flush 73d590b4bd), CASE/BCASE removed (3578bdf3c3, ARM 8d478e845c).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.5 — Done: 26bbe7ac9b, 18d9ddc35c, 02c1a9d87d, 6e3a2a3f9f, ef49b4ca78, a175fa3bc3, 72f8102244, 888d44d3c1, 0f27b91522, 54789eff38, 3952057cf6, 034a10d44c, 467a2cb73c. Left open: “No peep optimizer yet”, no shared linking.
  • Go 1.6 — Done: 3a9bc571b0, 72180c3b82, 3534e2bef4, 80d9106487, 2a031e6a2a, 73d590b4bd, 3578bdf3c3, 61a3ebed55, 5f23bc8903.

The mips64 port and the mips/mips64 register space

Design. The port was built the same way as arm64 by copying ppc64: cmd/internal/obj/mips first as a mechanical copy “to reduce code difference when adding the mips64 port” (5cc86c6f55), cmd/compile/internal/mips64 likewise (14f919578d), then real support for GOARCH=mips64{,le} in obj (fa6a1ecd63), cmd/asm (43ea305435) and the compiler (d5cd4ab46a, 689 insertions / 1129 deletions relative to the copy). Register space was reduced afterwards (1b6d55acab).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.6 — Done: the above. Left open: nothing noted besides that the port starts with the ppc64 structure.

Native Client (nacl/386, nacl/amd64p32, nacl/arm) and amd64p32 in the toolchain

Span: Go 1.3 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: not covered by this range’s commits after 1.5

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc Go 1.3 Native Client Support cited in this thread's commits

Design. The first merge was a mechanical import of Russ Cox’s NaCl branch (7c8280c9ef, per golang.org/s/go13nacl), followed by assembler/compiler support (7954b2b90b): consult $GOARCH, and in 6c under NaCl “some of the more complex addressing modes must be disabled, and the BP and R15 registers must not be used”. amd64p32 (32-bit pointers on amd64) required linkarchinit in cc and gc (d4896fb876, e31a1ce109), 6a support (e509bbc943), morestack fixes (9460cf7825), stack alignment fixes (3d5e219e02), correct stack zeroing (741244e433, bfbb2e827b, ac0e12d158), and Duff’s device disabled (c6a41a3559). nacl/386 (88f84b3e41) and nacl/arm (783bcba84d, large stack offsets 782eea0190) followed.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.3 — Done: 7c8280c9ef, 7954b2b90b, d4896fb876, e31a1ce109, e509bbc943, 9460cf7825, 88f84b3e41, 741244e433, bfbb2e827b, c6a41a3559, 3d5e219e02. Left open: working NaCl support not included in the first merge (“does not include working NaCl support”).
  • Go 1.4 — Done: nacl/arm (783bcba84d), ac0e12d158, 8a7597fd7a.
  • Go 1.5 — Done: amd64p32 build fixes (12079acaa0, cbc854a799), nacl/arm stack offsets (782eea0190).

Position-independent code, dynamic linking and TLS in the assemblers

Span: Go 1.3 → Go 1.6 · Status at go1.17: working on amd64, 386, arm, arm64, ppc64le → continues as Prologue, frame pointer, stack split and function alignment (cmd/internal/obj) (1.18+)

Design. With liblink, TLS and shared-library rewrites became explicit assembler passes. 1.3: a TLS pseudo-register introduced for 386/amd64 so 4(GS)-style operands are rewritten in one place (90093f0634); 1.5: -shared re-enabled on amd64 with -shared flags in cmd/asm and 6g (09d9520be9), -shared TLS base computation on x86 (e73981512f, 14fbec49dc), -dynlink access to global data through the GOT (84207a2500), duffcopy/duffzero called via GOT (1d1c61ba7d), R15 freed when not needed for GOT indirection (8a3132dd5e), framepointer and prologue changes. 1.6: GOT access on arm (e6ceb92e1c), arm64 (3534e2bef4), ppc64le (2ac993107f) and 386 (cb0393866a, 342f17eaf7), independent bits of toolchain TLS support (9e6ba37b86, 7bf959c67a), “a saner model for TLS on arm” (b0344e9fd5), native-ish TLS on arm64 (72180c3b82), initial-exec (80d9106487), IE on ppc64le (a35c85c0cc), regopt must not use CX in PIC on 386 (61da0e92d0, 9514285da9) and android/386 local-exec (0fbf0955d4), -shared/-dynlink on ppc64 (c23c8d58d6), x86 GOT rewrite factored (3c85e1b186). Solaris needed a way to avoid pc-relative addressing (4516a60062, 1.4).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.3 — Done: 90093f0634.
  • Go 1.4 — Done: 4516a60062.
  • Go 1.5 — Done: 09d9520be9, e73981512f, 14fbec49dc, 84207a2500, 1d1c61ba7d, 8a3132dd5e, 264858c46e, 0661143447.
  • Go 1.6 — Done: the list above. Left open: “the make TLS make sense project has quite a few more steps to go” (9e6ba37b86).
