Backends and assemblers (Go 1.12–1.17)

Reader: Claude Sonnet. Cites 883 of 988 commits in this slice; every non-noise commit is cited, plus 4 larger commits the noise filter had set aside, which a separate gap reader described. Read the design-heavy messages and subject lines. Most “Left open” entries say “nothing noted” because peephole commits rarely mention follow-ups.

Release digest for this slice
  • Go 1.12 — Dominated by incremental lowering work (amd64/386/ARM/arm64/ppc64/s390x peepholes), arm64 constants without the literal pool, arm64 frame pointers and the first symabis plumbing for the future register ABI.
  • Go 1.13 — Intrinsics and ports: Add64/Sub64 carry chains, wasm intrinsics and options, ABI wrappers for linkname’d symbols, index-carrying bounds failures, s390x sequentially consistent atomics.
  • Go 1.14 — riscv64 assembler and compiler arrive; multi-control blocks and s390x compare-and-branch; FMA intrinsics; unsafe-point marking for async preemption; compiler-generated debug_lines; dev.link object format begins.
  • Go 1.15 — rulegen reshaped (ellipses, commutative loops, typed aux); separate addressing-modes pass for amd64/386/s390x; stack maps only at calls; spectre mitigation; alignment directives; new object format re-enabled.
  • Go 1.16 — typed aux finished everywhere; late call expansion (AuxCall); 387 removed, softfloat added; arm64 SHA/atomics/SIMD; riscv64 g moved to X27 with PIE; content-addressable symbols; register maps deleted.
  • Go 1.17 — Register-based ABI on amd64 (X15, R14, wrappers, expand_calls, spills) delivered with dev.regabi package split; depth-first block layout; arm64 conditional-select rules; memmove inlining; large clean-up of ppc64 assembler optab.

Register-based ABI (ABIInternal) and ABI wrappers

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: amd64 passes arguments and results in registers by default, with ABI0↔︎ABIInternal wrappers generated by the compiler; R14 = g, X15 = zero, R12/R13 = entry scratch; other architectures still stack-based → continues as Register-based calling convention (ABIInternal) ports beyond amd64 (1.18+)

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc Proposal: Register-based Go calling convention Austin Clements, 2020-08-10 · linked from #40724
  • proposal #40724 cmd/compile: switch to a register-based calling convention for Go functions referenced by 35 of this thread's commits
  • design doc Proposal: Create an undefined internal calling convention Austin Clements, 2019-01-14 · linked from #31230
  • proposal #27539 proposal: runtime: make the ABI undefined as a step toward changing it referenced by 6 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #18597 proposal: cmd/compile: define register-based calling convention linked from #27539
  • tracking issue #44816 cmd/compile: register ABI bringup testcase failures (tracking issue) referenced by 4 of this thread's commits
  • discussion Bug in new amd64 ABI golang-dev · linked from #40724
  • background Go internal ABI specification. listed in Go: A Documentary

Design. The work starts from a naming problem rather than a register file: assembly functions are ABI0 (all arguments on the stack), Go functions are to become ABIInternal, and the toolchain must know which symbol is which. In 1.12 Austin Clements adds the plumbing: cmd/asm -symabis runs the assembler in a fast, lax “collect symbol definition/reference ABIs” mode (ba2e8a629b), the compiler accepts and parses the resulting symabis file (97e4010fd4), and later the compiler stops conflating data and function LSyms so that a symbol looked up before it is known to be a function is not silently ABI0 (a2e79571a9). In 1.13 the compiler generates ABI wrappers for //go:linkname’d symbols (b402bd4499), replacing a hack in cmd/go that scanned related packages when building the runtime’s symabis, and the -allabis mode is removed (74d92db8d7). In 1.16 the assembler learns explicit <ABI0>/<ABIInternal> selectors on definitions and references, enabled only for runtime-related packages (dd58239dd2), and cmd/dist/cmd/go define an asm macro GOEXPERIMENT_REGABI for the runtime, reflect, syscall and runtime/internal/* (4d1cecdee8).

The real implementation happens on dev.regabi and ships in 1.17. Wrappers are created as real IR (not ABI aliases): initially “no-op” wrappers that call the target using the existing ABI, on the assumption that late call expansion can later expand the call for both ABI0 and ABIInternal (cb28c96be8). GOEXPERIMENT=regabi is then split into regabiwrappers, regabig, regabireflect, regabidefer, regabiargs (eaa1ddee84), replacing the -abiwrap flag, so that wrappers can be benchmarked without the new register convention (bf5fa2d198). Register assignment lives in abiutils (refactored out of gc into package abi, c41b999ad4; updated for the revised ABI, 5a76c3d548; ABI info plumbed into ssagen/ssa and expandCalls, 7a2f3273c5, d0d21b7c4c). AMD64 parameter registers and OpArgIntReg/OpArgFloatReg ops were plumbed into ssa.Config (74cac8d479), with morestack spill support copied from the original experiment CL (c1370e918f).

Special registers: X15 is reserved as constant zero in ABIInternal and used to zero memory, re-zeroed on ABI0→ABIInternal transitions (401d7e5a24; fixed use for frame zeroing 1678829d95, zerorange made regabi-friendly 3300390ec7, c26f954a54, b2389ad3ce); R14 is the g register (5d7dc53888) with the assembler told about it (397a46a10a) and the obj/x86 stack-bound check reading it (2e60c00f56); R12/R13 become REGENTRYTMP0/1 for WRAPPER prologues because BX/DI are now argument registers (87c6fa4f47, 2ebe77a2fd). The assembler requires NOSPLIT for ABIInternal asm functions (25b25a9ed7) and omits args_stackmap for them (4480c822ba). Functions with cgo_unsafe_args are pinned to ABI0 (6996bae5d1). Wrapper vs. ABIWrapper flags are untangled (5cc5576a9c).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: -symabis collection mode in cmd/asm (ba2e8a629b), compiler parsing of symabis (97e4010fd4), separation of data and function LSyms (a2e79571a9). Left open: the information is parsed but “doesn’t yet do anything” (97e4010fd4).
  • Go 1.13 — Done: ABI wrappers for linkname’d symbols (b402bd4499); -allabis mode removed (74d92db8d7). Left open: wrappers are aliases for the stack ABI only; no register convention exists.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: asm ABI selectors for runtime packages (dd58239dd2); GOEXPERIMENT_REGABI asm macro (4d1cecdee8); -S=2 dumps symbol ABI versions (982ac06f3d); the late call expansion groundwork (see next thread); cmd/go/asm get -linkshared plumbing (56b783ad94). Left open: no register assignment in the compiler yet.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: [dev.regabi] ABI wrappers as IR (cb28c96be8), morestack spill support (c1370e918f), AMD64 parameter register defs and Arg ops (74cac8d479), abiutils refactor and plumbing (c41b999ad4, 5a76c3d548, 7a2f3273c5, d0d21b7c4c), X15/R14 reservations (401d7e5a24, 5d7dc53888, 397a46a10a, 2e60c00f56), register args retrieved from registers (f2df1e3c34), passed to callees (4532467c18), simple register results for ints and strings (9d88a9e2bf), aggregate OpArg in registers (9f33dc3ca1), morestack handling (a2d92b5143, 3778f8e07d, b6e1c33603), results loaded into registers on the open-defer return path (f5efa5a313), output parameters passed in registers spilled as autos (8ed438c077, fixed 0ec2c4abba), partially-live argument spilling reworked to occur after liveness (23f8c203f0) and spills placed after OpArg{Int,Float}Reg (56af34f875, a690a5d75f), frame offsets checked against the ABI (5ff7ec98b7, 97b32a6724), redundant register moves reduced in call setup by allocating inputs in a better order (6b8e3e2d06), reflect.callReflect/callMethod wrappers not clobbering arguments (3711ea0b5d), struct field padding in register-passed structs (d19eece91f), several offset/trailing-empty-field fixes (998fe70b68, 98dfdc82c8, 5f646f0a98, 45ca9ef5c1, 052da5717e, 382851c1fd, 14ef2d8c01, d6f6ef6358), the five-way experiment split (eaa1ddee84). Cross-checked with git log: the five sub-experiments (and regabiargs) were switched on by default for amd64 in April 2021 (9dd71ba913, fd3612e433, bbb510ccc9, 88655480f3, af8a176e91; Android 9c12f1b433). Left open: only amd64 (regabiSupported); ABI0 vs ABIInternal still gated by experiment machinery; all non-amd64 ports remain stack-based.

Late call expansion, AuxCall and the expand_calls pass

Span: Go 1.16 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: default design: calls carry *ssa.AuxCall, and expand_calls lowers arguments/results (including registers) after generic optimization → continues as Register-based calling convention (ABIInternal) ports beyond amd64 (1.18+)

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #40724 cmd/compile: switch to a register-based calling convention for Go functions referenced by 6 of this thread's commits
  • design doc Proposal: Register-based Go calling convention Austin Clements, 2020-08-10 · linked from #40724

Design. Before 1.16, SSA call values carried an *obj.LSym (static) or nothing (closure/interface) in Aux, and argument/result marshalling was built during SSA generation as explicit stack stores/loads. To make the register ABI possible and to allow interprocedural SSA optimization, David Chase moves the lowering of call ABI details later. First a dedicated Aux type: *ssa.AuxCall substitutes 1-for-1 for the LSym in static calls (b4ef49e527), is extended to closure and interface calls (3c85e995ef) and populated for OpClosureCall (39da81da5e). New ops for the experiment — Dereference, StaticLECall, SelectN, SelectNAddr — arrive in 35e413c537; 44c0586931 adds the code to expand calls just before “late opt”. 15f01d6ae9 delays expansion of OpArg itself until expand_calls, merges two overlapping functions in expand_calls.go into one called twice, drops the per-function GOSSAHASH dependence and keeps a go116lateCallExpansion kill switch.

In 1.17 the pass is extended in step with regabi: StaticCall returns a “Results” value (e25040d162), return values are expanded late (92cb157cf3), ABIInfo is plumbed through (d0d21b7c4c), expandCalls preserves types of pointer stores (ca3aefc4a9), and a recursive-invalidate Value method is added for it (a9e475a15a). A kill switch (c78c79f152) was activated after a regression in 1.16 (the “revert switch”); a separate fix addresses interface-typed OpIData loads (92c732e901), a “leaf type” bug for singleton register-sized structs (f8d80977b7), and Arg scheduling (cb42e3e979). OpArg values that arrive in registers are scheduled first.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.16 — Done: AuxCall introduced (b4ef49e527, 3c85e995ef, 39da81da5e), new LE ops (35e413c537), expansion before late opt (44c0586931), OpArg expansion delayed (15f01d6ae9), regression switch (c78c79f152), correct leaf type (f8d80977b7). Left open: still guarded by go116lateCallExpansion; results are not expanded late.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: Results-returning StaticCall (e25040d162), late return expansion (92cb157cf3), integration with abi info (d0d21b7c4c), AuxCall.args made redundant and removed (a93849b9e2), type-preserving stores (ca3aefc4a9), recursive invalidation (a9e475a15a), OpArg scheduling (cb42e3e979), Aux marker interface ssa.Aux (1a98ab0e2d) with ir.Node conversions rewritten to *ir.Name (6db970e20a, dcec658f6c). Left open: nothing noted beyond the architecture ports.

dev.regabi package decomposition (ssagen, liveness, objw, types, abi)

Span: Go 1.17 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: done; gc no longer holds SSA generation or liveness → continues in the 1.18+ compiler layout

Design. In the 1.17 cycle, the [dev.regabi] branch used mechanically generated (rf, [git-generate]) refactors to break package gc apart, so the backend could be handled without import cycles (“gc ↔︎ ssa cycle hacks” removed, 048debb224). Known symbols/packages/names move to package ir (65c4c6dfb2), type size computation moves to package types (dac0de3748), object writing to objw (0ced54062e), liveness to its own package (071ab0a14c, with ir.Node use eliminated in b75f51c645, 9eeed291bc), SSA generation to ssagen (6c34d2f420), and dependencies flattened (3383b5c74a). Stack objects move into liveness (422f38fb6c); Addrconst/Patch set up to move into obj (2153a99914). LocalSlot.N becomes *ir.Name (dcec658f6c). Fixes for the big rewrite are in d1d1099c91.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.17 — Done: all of the above hashes. Left open: nothing noted.

Rewrite-rule generator (rulegen): ellipses, commutativity loops, typed aux

Span: Go 1.13 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: all rule files use typed aux/auxint (=>); commutative ops use nested loops; no chunking → continues in the 1.18+ SSA rule infrastructure

Earlier history: Rewrite-rule machinery and compile-time performance of the SSA compiler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. cmd/compile/internal/ssa/gen/*.rules compile into huge Go switch functions. By 1.14–1.15 the generated files (about 190 KiB less in 870080752d) were hurting editor and build time. The series by Josh Bleecher Snyder shrank them: more precise prediction of “magic” variables b, config, fe, typ removed ~3000 pointless _ = lines (53948127d3); early tweaks to for-loop shape (0fbf681840, 04b8a9fea5), package-level shadowing fixes (9f56845f2c), block rewrite code size reduced with Block.Reset (c7d81bc086, 5e4da0adac). Commutative ops: previously one rule per argument permutation; bd6d78ef37 instead generates nested loops that try both orderings, preceded by the fix that generates commutative variants when a condition mentions the arguments (73269b8e75) and a63ed10d44 skipping (Op x x). Bounds checks in generated code are cut by preloading v.Args[0]/[1] and swapping in the loop post statement (a3f234c706, a2bff7c296); chunking is removed (6dd11bcb35); AddArgN helpers shrink the compiler binary by about 192 KB (7913f7dfcf), and d98e0720bc regenerates. Also “ellipsis” rules (Op ...) => (Op2 ...) for ops that map one-to-one are adopted architecture by architecture: 386 (7c0f540b00), ARM (5749c0eb5b), ARM64 (2bfa8c37c3), MIPS (1bda9b001f), wasm (088aad5ff6), dec64 (5abab1da2c), PPC64 (3abec31097), S390X (3a9381c6b0), MIPS64 (49db4ae40f), RISCV64 (2ed96d0958), AMD64 (a37bbcecca). RHS common subexpressions are CSE’d (67a8660b5a). 390c096ee9 makes clobber variadic; 5437b5a24b rejects rules that declare reserved names; 4ebb6f5110 automates resultInArg0 register checks; bd8b3fe5be shrinks no-op rewrite funcs.

Typed aux (Keith Randall): Aux and AuxInt were interface{} and int64; every rule cast. 28157b3292 makes the generator declare the real types per opcode, using => for strongly typed rules and -> for legacy rules so that migration can proceed rule file by rule file. It introduces a Sym type instead of interface{} for symbolic offsets (ea7126fe14) and ARM64BitField aux (2cf3ebaf3d), ValAndOff accessors return int32 (b70a2bc9c6), CCop aux for arm64 conditional ops (ffbd8524ac, ae658cb19a). Migration commits: amd64 (2f84caebe3, dc9879e8fd, f0c7e3e946, 0f82e58392, fa63d24333, 66fbb80b72, b6632f770f, 83e8bf2e7d, 0f55d37d44, 9a7a981ab7, 39a426d356), 386 (bbaae9c43d, 17fbc818ff, a95bf77e1a), wasm (82f29898ea), riscv64 (7004be998b), mips64 (67d40873ad, 4e4d5df0b0), mips (81df5e69fc, e47a17aeee), s390x (b1cae8cd1d, b7a5e7ae92, 925d6b31b0, f639a81cd5, e1a96b82df, 1d9801223e, 03eb7e20e4), arm64 (ac211c037d, c53d1236df, 70d9b72a87, bd01a1b756, c8b42f9aa5, 666c9aedd4, b3c0fe1d14, 328214e85c, 85902b6786, ea33523877), ARM in eight parts (c9551f9c19, 7f7184686b, be01f54c24, bfe72ec56a, d2bd93a010, 150bd4ffd4, 1f41f04d2c, aacbd7c3aa, 58fa8075f5, f5c3eda4c9, 3ca3ca51d7, 9ec0a46a15, 0eb52ac250), dec/dec64/decArgs (917aa72c14, 7f0c479fff, f1a2a0e0bf) and splitload (bf5b83a835). 1e820a3432 ensures ... rules have compatible aux types. Cleanups: 5c1122b528, bc0d7fd9b7, de2d1c3fe2, 1af388f1c0.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.13 — Done: magic-variable prediction tightened (53948127d3), for-loop verbosity (0fbf681840), stopping the shadowing of the bool type in rules (9f56845f2c), 07b4b4a1a8 adds a scale field to SSA ops. Left open: generated files still huge.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: output reduced by 200 KiB (870080752d), block-rewrite code reduced (c7d81bc086), minor simplifications (bdf0fe5448). Left open: commutative expansion still permutation-per-rule.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: ellipsis rules across all ports; commutative loops (bd6d78ef37) with preceding correctness fixes (73269b8e75, a63ed10d44, 49f8d45994); HMUL marked non-commutative on amd64 because rulegen could not yet express the asymmetric rules without infinite loops (6817210edf); bounds checks cut (a3f234c706); chunking removed (6dd11bcb35); AddArgN (7913f7dfcf); typed aux begins (28157b3292, ea7126fe14) and 386/s390x/mips/wasm/riscv64/dec ports start. Left open: arm64, ARM, amd64, s390x partially migrated.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: ARM, ARM64, AMD64, s390x, mips64 rule files completed; =>-only enforcement for ARM; aacbd7c3aa. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: reserved-name check (5437b5a24b), resultInArg0 check automation (4ebb6f5110), ValAndOff int32 (b70a2bc9c6), explicit Aux match in store-combining rule (a829114b21, which notes a TODO to require Aux/AuxInt to be always specified on the LHS), smaller no-op rewrite funcs (bd8b3fe5be). Left open: the a829114b21 message flags the “unspecified aux is ignored in matching” behaviour as error-prone.

amd64 lowering: read-modify-write, load-op, addressing modes pass, intrinsic-friendly rules

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: still the design at go1.17 → continues as amd64 code generation and GOAMD64 microarchitecture levels (1.18+)

Earlier history: amd64 and 386 instruction selection (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. The amd64 rules fuse loads and stores into x86’s memory-operand forms. In 1.12 Ben Shi and others add DIVSSload/DIVSDload (705f3c74e6), more read-modify-write ops (b75c5c5992, 3bc34385fa: AND/SUB/OR/XOR with memory destination and constant sources), BTSLconstmodify-style bit ops (c6bf9a8109), ADDQconstmodify to DEC (5f5ea3fd4d), load/store combining on 386/amd64 (95dda75bde), “prefer rematerializeable arg0 for HMUL” (24e51bbe64), splitting slow 3-operand LEAs: objdump counts LEA.*(.*(.* 1012 → 20 in go (b40db51438), and folding address calculations into CMPload[const] ops (b1f656b1ce, with 623c772814 fixing the CMPconstload rule and 9f291d1fc3 a load/compare combining rule).

By 1.15 the explosion of rule orderings needed to find complicated addressing modes (x+y, x+2*y) is replaced with a separate pass: ordinary load/store rules only carry a constant offset and symbol; 98cb76799c adds a pass that combines loads with LEAQx ops, shrinking the diffstat by ~5000 lines (3145 insertions, 8176 deletions). The same pass was later applied to 386 (reverted and retried because it created transient out-of-bounds pointers: af7eafd150, d84cbec890, 3adbdb6d99, 5b897ec017), and s390x (17ae587383). Indexed load+op (882ec701d2), indexed memory modification (9ed0fb42e3), indexed CMP loads (bba88467f8, e4e192484b), faultOnNilArg0 forbidden for indexed forms (287d67e3dd). The pass was extended with floating-point load+op (c4fed25553).

Other amd64 work: LoweredHasCPUFeature intrinsic (fff7509d47, MOVBQZX version 7ee8467b27), preferring AND to SHR+SHL pairs when masking (4e2b84ffc5, f41451e7eb), unsigned compares to 0/1 (18053b7131), shift pairs merged into stores (f53f987ebf), ADDQ instead of LEAQ (1cfe8e91b6), constant store merging (9c60094986, f510cddcd1, ba0e651130), MOVO of readonly sym with immediates (f5b5d77ee2), multi-register shifts SHLD/SHRD (43d5f213e2), arch-specific runtime.memmove inlining on amd64/arm64 (3b321a9d12), adding more registers for write-barrier calls (8114242359, with wrapper variants of runtime.gcWriteBarrier per second-argument register), readonly-global loads into constants (653a4bd8d4), x & 1 != 0 (e7c1873691), and a correction for long RMW bit ops (359f44910f) after which the BT{S,R,C}modify ops are removed as slower than the fallbacks (b211fe0058). Spectre mitigation -spectre=index uses CMOV to prevent speculation past bounds checks (877ef86bec), and -spectre=ret adds return-trampoline mode (fc8a6336d1).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: RMW/loadop work above (705f3c74e6, b75c5c5992, 3bc34385fa, c6bf9a8109, 5f5ea3fd4d, b40db51438, 24e51bbe64, b1f656b1ce, 623c772814), MULQ overflow intrinsics (a1ca4893ff), RotateLeft (5ac2476748), simplify asm generators (4545fea4fc, d17ac29158, 2294e3ebd3, ccc337d8ee), correction of load-compare combination (9f291d1fc3). Left open: address mode rules are order-sensitive.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: a SETcc-store rule typed incorrectly is corrected (23f3ea82b9); no other amd64-specific design work. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: FMA intrinsic via VFMADD231SD guarded by cpu.X86.HasFMA (7a6da218b1), AND-over-shifts (4e2b84ffc5, f41451e7eb), amd64p32 rules removed (b12703e052, ce49f9506a). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: addressing-modes pass (98cb76799c), HasCPUFeature (fff7509d47), spectre (877ef86bec, fc8a6336d1), 386 conversion. Left open: 386 pass first reverted (5b897ec017).
  • Go 1.16 — Done: And/Or atomic intrinsic (44dbeaf356), typed-aux completion (39a426d356). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: memmove inlining (3b321a9d12), multi-register shifts (43d5f213e2), BT-modify removal (b211fe0058), RMW fix (359f44910f), store coalescing (bf48163e8f). Left open: b211fe0058 leaves “which fallback strategy is better” as TBD.

arm64 backend and assembler

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: mature backend with constant synthesis by MOVZ/MOVK and ADD pairs, frame pointer on by default, ARMv8.1 atomics; → continues as arm64 code generation and assembler (1.18+)

Earlier history: ARM and ARM64 instruction selection and fused operations (Go 1.8 → Go 1.11) · ARM64 assembler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Two parallel streams: assembler improvements in cmd/internal/obj/arm64 (asm7.go, literal pools) and compiler rewrite rules. The assembler stopped using the constant pool for most values: large 64-bit constants are encoded as MOVZ/MOVN plus MOVK sequences (644ddaa842), 32/64-bit constants are reclassified by opcode width (86ce1cb060), float constants that chipfloat7() can encode go to FMOVS/FMOVD immediates (c430adf136), ADD $0x123456 is split into two shifted-immediate ADDs (808186203b), and stack addresses with big offsets are done with two ADD/one SUB rather than a pool load (a86b6f23f0). Pool size accounting is fixed in 1.17 (d25476ebb2, 9c7207891c). Frame pointers are supported on arm64 (8f4fd3f34e): FP saved on the word below RSP; runtime assembly, wrappers and scheduler adjusted; stack-overflow check in the linker takes the extra word into account; nosplit tests changed for 16-byte frame alignment; enabled by default on Linux but disabled with GOEXPERIMENT=noframepointer; later “framepointers are no longer an experiment - hard code them” (5c2c6d3fbf, 1.16). The epilogue is made async-signal safe (47232f0d92), LR is saved after SP decrement on darwin (13fb147e60), small stack functions are marked NOSPLIT (d8394bfc7f) and huge-frame prologue simplified (4702dd67a7).

On the compiler side, arm64 grows MADD/MSUB fusion (b444215116, d60cf39f8e), shifted-operand forms (5aeecc4530), TST/CMN comparison forms (0e9f1de0b7), indexed FP loads/stores (3ca3e89bb6, 84feb4bbb7), float<->int moves for Float64bits (a19a83c8ef), Copysign (2e5c32518c), RoundToEven and Abs (8149db4f64), non-constant ROR (204cc14bdd), FCMP with zero (27cce773d3) and a change of the flag conditions for floating-point comparisons (6efd51c6b7) later followed by a wrong-complement fix for CSEL (d9b79e53bb), REV16 for ReverseBytes16 (192b675f17, b182ba7fab), CLZW for Len32 (dd91269b7c), Add64/Sub64 (5714c91b53, f8f265b9cf, d0cbf9bf53) and Div32 (159b2de442), EON (01aad9ea93), unsigned comparison to 0/1 (06337823ef), conditional-instruction rules CSETM/CSINC/CSINV/CSNEG (f5e6d3e879, bug fix 8d77e45064), single-precision square root (2b50ab2aee), float slice access (3ee32439b5), MOV nop folding (d2911d7612) and rewrites to constant 0 (3a0061822e). Overflow-correctness: comparisons-with-zero rewriting to CMN/CMP is wrong on overflow, so new LTnoov/GEnoov/LEnoov/GTnoov block kinds are introduced that ignore V (e8f5a33191, arm twin e031318ca6). ARMv8.1 atomics: LDADD*/LDAND*/LDEOR*/LDOR*/SWP* (448089854a, 26d62b4ca9, 1018a80fe8), CAS/CASP (15131caeaa), used by intrinsics guarded by a CPU-feature branch (ecc3f5112e, cdb19b4dba). New SIMD/crypto assembler support: VLD/VST 2-4 (8403d4ea90), VLD1-4R (2bf7a92571), SHA512 (93eeb819ca), SHA3 (3036b76df0), system registers (9c67516ed6, 9ce5cad0aa), PCALIGN (2f8798ed07), FLDPQ/FSTPQ (79beddc773), VDUP (9136d958ab), VUMAX/VUMIN (726d704c32).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: constant synthesis (644ddaa842, 86ce1cb060, c430adf136, 808186203b), indexed FP and atomics (84feb4bbb7, 1018a80fe8, 26d62b4ca9), FRINTND/Abs/Copysign/Float bits (8149db4f64, 2e5c32518c, a19a83c8ef), madd (b444215116), frame pointer (8f4fd3f34e). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: v8.1 atomics (448089854a), bits intrinsics (5714c91b53, f8f265b9cf, dd91269b7c, 159b2de442, 4e2b0dda8c, 192b675f17), FCMP $0 (27cce773d3), changed FP flags (6efd51c6b7), TSTW fix (2ef8abb41f), 4ea7aa7cf3 uses R20/R21 in Duff’s devices. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: vector LD/ST (8403d4ea90), system registers (9c67516ed6, 9ce5cad0aa), unsafe-point marking (4736088463), NOOP (3876bd67ef, 01f15b62b3), no REGTMP in ZeroRange (0f992b9948). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: PCALIGN (2f8798ed07), prologue_end stmt (a88c26eb28), typed aux started, rev16 (2783249068), ARM64 compare redo of flag consts (a07e28194a), VCNT fix (e5e386938f). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: SHA512/SHA3/SIMD instructions (93eeb819ca, 3036b76df0, d7ab277eed, 3089ef6bd7, dfdc3880b0, fa04d488bd, 5d0b35ca98), CAS (15131caeaa), atomic And/Or/swap intrinsics (cdb19b4dba, ecc3f5112e), darwin/arm64 PIE and c-shared (234de9e1c2, f8e554021b, b85c2dd56c), call reloc fix (3f7b4d1207), unsigned compare to 0/1 (06337823ef), EON (01aad9ea93), VMOVQ fix (cd99385ff4), frame pointers made unconditional (5c2c6d3fbf), a86b6f23f0. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: conditional-select rules (f5e6d3e879), REV16 (b182ba7fab), float slices (3ee32439b5), inlined memmove (3b321a9d12), 128-bit FP pair loads (79beddc773), extended register ops with RSP (a607408403, 355c3a037e), shift-amount range checks (0636d88f6d, 9726c78539), R16/R17 and R12 clobber marks for special calls (11b4aee05b, 4a7effa418), encoding fixes (48b7432e3f, 5daefc5363, f439a76253, c925e1546e, e2e05af6e1, a6a853f94c, 27dbc4551a), small-stack NOSPLIT (d8394bfc7f), huge-frame prologue (4702dd67a7). Left open: nothing noted.

riscv64 port: assembler and compiler

Span: Go 1.14 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: working linux/riscv64 with PIE and cgo, atomics, Duff’s devices, branch pseudo-instructions → continues as riscv64 compiler and assembler (RVA profiles, vector, compressed) (1.18+)

Design docs & discussion
  • tracking issue #27532 all: port to RISC-V referenced by 21 of this thread's commits

Design. Based on the external riscv-go port (Updates #27532). The assembler in cmd/internal/obj/riscv was imported in layers: arch definition in cmd/internal/sys (a3ceb57fb4), instruction and register definitions generated from the riscv-opcodes parse_opcodes tables (7ef890db91), consolidated LinkArch handling in cmd/asm (112a72a020), a framework supporting raw WORDs (6c6ad3086e), then computational (c3c53661ba, e29d276d55), environment call/breakpoint and counters (ced2454220), load/store/multiply (dfbc9c83a9), floating point (434e4caf1b), AUIPC/LUI (430d2aa349), control transfer (a37f2b4f60), MOV pseudo-instructions (a04aa1f6d1, 24902c5be6), immediate splitting (8cf5293caa, 1424889921, d8e052667f), call/jmp/branch handling (7cab55dfd3), prologue/epilogue (6718cb617f), archreloc for the linker (1046a9cb1b), shortened call sequence (a50c3ffbd4). The compiler backend landed in one commit with 8680 insertions (98d2717499). 1.15 reworks instruction generation to emit multiple instructions from one Prog rather than rewriting Progs (3e00061f52), stores relocation details in Prog.RestArgs (2b920cba8f), and adds LR/SC (85a8526a7e), AMO (10635921e5), FCLASS (32dbccde78), branch pseudo-instructions (a3d8c210ad), NOT/NEG/NEGW (dc3255391a, 25da2ea72c). Compiler rules: multi-control (compare-and-branch) blocks (40f2dab0e1), branch optimization (57e32c4fbd), absorbing SNEZ (c9ece81cc8), immediates (97585092f5), zero stores (cc6a8bd0d7), atomic intrinsics for Load8/Load32/Load64/Store*/Add/Cas/Exchange (2e918c3aab, ade988623e, efb0ac4ce6), And/Or (497feff168), and ReturnBlock fix (ed91661745). In 1.16 the g register moves from TP/X4 to X27 so that cgo and TLS can coexist (6f45b39e4d), Duff’s devices are used (150d2448e5), PIE and extra build modes are enabled (4f2d213476, 8eb846fd37), sign/zero-extension elimination removes “almost another 8,000 instructions from the go binary” (320cc79002, 8a013233ac, 12a2e72065) by changing Eq16/Neq16 to extend each operand before subtracting, and small zeroing/moves are optimized (0be8280d8d). In 1.17: single const MOV operand (6517844129), >32-bit constants loaded from memory (c2d625168f), sign-correct constants (8fd0f83552), JMP name<>(SB) (6fe8981620), constant load targets (0398a771d2), regabi unaffected.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.14 — Done: the assembler layers and compiler as above (a3ceb57fb4 through 98d2717499), linker reloc (1046a9cb1b), DWARF register map (fb8cdb7e4b). Left open: cgo unsupported (g in TP clash, later 6f45b39e4d1.16); PIE not enabled.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: instruction generation rework, atomics, compare-and-branch, pseudo-ops (listed above). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: g moved to X27 (6f45b39e4d), Duff’s devices, PIE/buildmodes, extension elimination (320cc79002), 8b51798304 removes X27 and S11 register names, branch-pseudo fix (0433845ad1), MOV for extensions (8a013233ac). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: constant materialization (6517844129, c2d625168f, 8fd0f83552), IsNonNil (125eca0f72), Eq32/Neq32 zero-extend before subtraction (c584f42dcf), huge-frame prologue (042f4cbb6f), atomics And/Or (497feff168). Left open: nothing noted.

PPC64 / POWER backend and assembler

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: power8 baseline with power9 instructions under GOPPC64=power9 → continues as PPC64 / Power10 backend (GOPPC64, prefixed instructions, PC-relative code) (1.18+)

Earlier history: Multi-architecture SSA ports: PPC64, MIPS64, MIPS32, s390x (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · 32-bit ARM, MIPS and PPC64 assemblers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Lynn Boger, Carlos Eduardo Seo, Paul E. Murphy and Cherry Zhang. Compiler: zero/sign-extension elimination and truncate fixes (8dbd9afbb0, d585f04fd3), indexed loads/stores (85c9c85955), shifts using bounded info (d45f24c084), record-form ANDCC/ORCC/XORCC to avoid CMP (4ae49b5921), intrinsics (Mul 9aed4cc395; TrailingZeros16/OnesCount8/16 23578f9d00; RotateLeft f2a18b1456; Add64 50ad09418e; CNTTZW/CNTTZD for POWER9 3023d7da49), VSX loads/stores in LoweredMove/Zero (816ff44479) then LXV/STXV and “Short” variants that don’t loop or clobber address registers on power9 (815509ae31), ISEL for variable shifts (a1550d3ca3), mod instructions on power9 (56933fb838), MADDLD (e7c7ce646f), SUBFIC (7615b20d06), combined rotate-mask shift rules (967465da29, c3c6fbf314), extswsli (a424f6e45e), MULLI (bdab5df40f), trunc fixes (cc2a5cf4b8), DS-form offset handling (ccf9acefa8, 6fbdfe4804, earlier 4-aligned folding). Assembler (obj/ppc64): VPERMXOR, DQ-form (lxv/stxv, 6b67f7d65d), PCALIGN 16/32 (bdba55653f, 37470c0664, c79c5e1aa4, 60a964ea45), float 0 via VSX (f776d51bf7), AND-based remainder (a3ef804891), vmrgow/vmrgew (8f79ca1d1a), lxvx/stxvx (64350f1eab), rlwnm and rldcr encodings (5ed81a3d14, d4aa72002e), 5-operand RLWNM/RLWMI (48ddf70128) and extra optab cleanup in 1.17 (2d30c94874, 1bad3831a0, 7bfe32f39c, 196b104bc1, 747f426944, a1a45afd4a, fca51ba24a, ddd8d7c0a6, 1eca6aa747, 06ac303f6a, 9bfa6f75d5, 4e16422da0). Indirect calls always go through LR so CTR is free for async preemption’s call injection (24e549a717), a hint on bclrl avoids a branch-predictor regression (cb674b5c13), R12 marked clobbered for write-barrier calls (b58d297416). Unsafe points marked (ceca99bdeb), MOVDU SP delta (3c47eada3f).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: rule improvements, indexed addressing, record-form compare avoidance, Mul/TrailingZeros/OnesCount intrinsics (see hashes above), float zero (f776d51bf7), PCALIGN (bdba55653f), AIX 64-bit addressing (041526c6ef, 4295ed9bef, 503091a77c, 20ac64a2dd). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: POWER9 CNTTZ (3023d7da49), RotateLeft (f2a18b1456), Add64 (50ad09418e), XX1-form encoding fix (259de39375), mid-stack-inlining NOP (2d3474043c, b098c0f467). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: DQ-form (6b67f7d65d), VSX moves (816ff44479), LR for indirect calls (24e549a717), unsafe points (ceca99bdeb), vmrg (8f79ca1d1a), AIX Duff (09c9bced82), ANDCC register masks (55924135ee). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: index fixes, move/zero improvements (815509ae31), ISEL shifts (a1550d3ca3), power9 mod (56933fb838), PCALIGN (37470c0664, c79c5e1aa4, 60a964ea45), shift constraints (daf39d06ee), NaN constants (78aa4af239), AND-remainder (a3ef804891). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: MADDLD, SUBFIC, combined shifts, EXTSWSLI, MULLI, bclrl hint (e7c7ce646f, 7615b20d06, 967465da29, a424f6e45e, bdab5df40f, cb674b5c13), TOC symbols static (076dc2111b), stop removing NOPs (7d7bd5abc7, 46ca7b5ee2). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: optab consolidation and DS-form handling (hash list above), 5-operand RLWNM (48ddf70128). Left open: nothing noted.

s390x backend: compare-and-branch, intrinsics, assembler

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: still stack ABI → continues as s390x, MIPS, 386 and 32-bit ARM backends (1.18+)

Earlier history: Multi-architecture SSA ports: PPC64, MIPS64, MIPS32, s390x (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Michael Munday’s chain: multiple SSA block control values (9c2e7e8bed) so a block can carry two register controls instead of one flags value; numeric condition-code masks stored as a Block field instead of one extended mnemonic per condition (cf03238020); then compare-and-branch rules (6ec4c71eef, object sizes -1.1% geomean, which also deleted loop_test.go in favour of a codegen test) and immediates optimization switching signedness for == and != so values fit an 8-bit immediate (e464d7d797, a58be734ea fixes shift-count type). Floating-point ops FADD/FSUB can yield flags (b2790a2838); float to uint conversions (2962c96c9f); store-multiple clobbers flags (a7a0f03050); int-float conversions clobber flags (377c1536f5). Intrinsics: OnesCount (6f9b94ab66, using popcnt then summing per-byte counts with pseudo ops), RotateLeft (f94de9c9fb), Add64/Sub64 via the condition code (2c1b5130aa, clobberFlags removed from loads/stores), Mul64 via MLGR (98aa97806b, ac2ceba01a), And8/Or8 via ‘rotate then xor selected bits’ with load-and-and/or (b3885dbc93, 646531c52a). Atomic loads/stores made sequentially consistent by serializing after stores (ac8dbe7747). Rotate-then-insert patterns (854e892ce1), addressing modes pass (17ae587383). Assembler: VMSLG variants (3f3142ad99), RNSBG/ROSBG/RXSBG/RISBG (0f79510dc5), IPM (6966b67510), SPM (1da575a7bc), branch-on-count (38c4a73706), masked branch and conditional load (8c99e45ef9), 12-bit load/store forms (90e0b40ab2), 2-byte NOP (11c2411c50), MVCIN (553a8626ba), ADDE memory (a45ea55da7), SYNC encoding (189931296f), inline marker fixes (d0d6593d1d, 268dd2e5a7).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: OnesCount, RotateLeft, 6f9b94ab66, f94de9c9fb, 4f15b54780 (int32 overflow in moves), abd1dde1f7 (no-op), VMSLG (3f3142ad99). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: atomic ordering (ac8dbe7747), Add64/Sub64 (2c1b5130aa), RISBG family (0f79510dc5), IPM (6966b67510), RestArgs (9c843f031d), optab param (e61985427e). Left open: spills of the carry per loop iteration noted in 2c1b5130aa (“may be able to reduce”).
  • Go 1.14 — Done: control values, numeric masks, compare-and-branch (above), Mul64 (98aa97806b, ac2ceba01a), And8/Or8 (b3885dbc93), sign extension removal (5c5f217b63). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: flag-producing FP ops (b2790a2838), simplified memory-operand rules (a03618500c), immediates (e464d7d797), typed rules. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: shift/mask (854e892ce1), addressing modes (17ae587383), strongly typed rules finished (03eb7e20e4), atomics And/Or (646531c52a). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: shift-count type fix (a58be734ea1.16). Left open: nothing noted.

386, ARM (32-bit), MIPS/MIPS64 and the 387 removal

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: maintenance; 387 dropped, GO386=softfloat for no-SSE → continues as s390x, MIPS, 386 and 32-bit ARM backends (1.18+)

Earlier history: Multi-architecture SSA ports: ARM, 386, ARM64 (dev.ssa) (Go 1.7 → Go 1.8) · 32-bit ARM, MIPS and PPC64 assemblers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. 386: load-op ops MULLload/DIVSSload/DIVSDload (90f2fa0037), OPC $imm,(mem) (a0a7e9fc0c), comparisons with memory (556971316f, 031a35ec84), indexed forms (3933302550, 27965c1436), load/store combination (4b78fe57a8), 387 simplifications (bd483592a2, e03220a594), TrailingZeros16 (22355d6cd2, 8d5197d818), conversion to the addressing-modes pass (above). ARM: comparisons (2b69ad0b3c, 285747b900, 067dfce21f), ARMv7 constants (0a382e0b7f), BFC (9f2411894b), ReverseBytes16 (fee84cc905), TrailingZeros (156c830bea), FMA via FMULAD (58b031949b), Abs (c683ab8128), RotateLeft32 (3cfd003a8a), NaCl DATABUNDLE removed (f6c624a22a), compare-with-zero overflow fix (e031318ca6), TST/TEQ do not set V (4826abb6c2), ARMv5 special case in regalloc removed (c4190fc34d). WebAssembly backend

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.16 · Status at go1.17: stack-based simulated registers with SP cached in locals, optional sign-extension/saturating ops via GOWASM → continues as WebAssembly backend (1.18+)

Earlier history: WebAssembly backend (Go 1.11 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc WebAssembly architecture for Go listed in Go: A Documentary

Design. Richard Musiol’s wasm port: the compiler emits Wasm with Go “registers” as Wasm globals, the stack in linear memory, and PC_F/PC_B globals to dispatch between functions. Improvements: locals count (6c631ae227), PC increments at sigpanic (52cae2763e), simpler zero extension (72d24a7484), math and math/bits intrinsics (5ee1b84959), optimized blocks in the binary (2396101e05), removal of the PC_F/PC_B globals (496b8dbbfc, by turning them into parameters and communicating through the Go stack), caching SP in a local per function (203e188837, to avoid V8’s slow global access; updated after each call), GOWASM=signext (4d23cbc671) and GOWASM=satconv (cf8cc7f63c, 42% faster, with helper fallbacks), Select (731e6fc34e), eliminated redundant extension/wrapping (1786ecd502), float32 registers (1c50fcf853), rotate and bounded shifts (b003afe4fe, b38be35e4c, 8fedb2d338, b9ef4c0f56), if-block optimization (9c384cc570), readonly globals (7be97af2ff), fast path for ULEB128 (03bb3e9ad1), deferred nil function panic (c4817f5d4f), refactored variable handling (547021d723), unsigned compare (8acbe4c0b3).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: 6c631ae227, 52cae2763e. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: intrinsics, GOWASM options, global/PC cleanup, SP caching (5ee1b84959, 4d23cbc671, cf8cc7f63c, 496b8dbbfc, 203e188837, 72d24a7484, 2396101e05). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: shift/rotate/bounded work and extension elimination (listed above). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: 8acbe4c0b3. Left open: nothing noted.

math/bits, atomic and runtime intrinsics (cross-architecture)

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: intrinsics for bits/atomic/FMA exist on most ports → continues as Atomics and memory-ordering code generation and Multi-word arithmetic, intrinsics and carry-chain support (1.18+)

Earlier history: Intrinsics for atomics, math/bits, math and runtime helpers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #25819 math: add guaranteed FMA referenced by 3 of this thread's commits

Design. Intrinsics are SSA ops generated from ssagen’s table. Carry chains use per-arch Add64/Sub64 lowerings that keep the carry in flags: amd64 (899f3a2892, dd789550a7: “individual ops are a bit slower but using the ops in carry chains is very fast”), arm64, ppc64x, s390x. A generic FMA op with arch rules (33425ab8db; amd64 7a6da218b1, arm 58b031949b), plus a rule not to use it on plan9 (03fb1f607b). runtime/internal/math.MulUintptr is an intrinsic on 386/amd64 using MUL and the overflow flag (a1ca4893ff: MulUintptr/large 10.7ns to 1.1ns) and on MIPS64 (ab7ecea0c8). Atomics: Load8 (4a4e05b0b1), Store8 (97592b3c14), And/Or on several ports in 1.16 (44dbeaf356, cdb19b4dba, e223c6cf07, 646531c52a, e5ad73508e, riscv64 in 1.17 497feff168). Division invariants: unsigned divisibility via modular inverse (a28a942768, from Granlund–Montgomery and Hacker’s Delight) and signed (6b1d5471b9).

SSA infrastructure passes: layout, regalloc, scheduling, flagalloc, block shape

Span: Go 1.12 → Go 1.17 · Status at go1.17: depth-first layout with exit-block placement, regalloc using phi/desired info → continues as Register allocator, scheduler and block-level backend passes (1.18+)

Earlier history: Register allocation, flag allocation and stack slots (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Scheduling, tighten, block layout and CFG passes (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. Block control: from 1.14 a block may have up to two control values (9c2e7e8bed); Block.Reset/AddControl streamline rewrite code (5e4da0adac). Flags: 80b6812d7b moves flagalloc op splitting to rewrite rules; dead values are removed after flagalloc (6303c34d7f); the go115flagallocdeadcode switch removed (91b7619310). Comparison argument order is canonicalized so CSE can merge them (44fe355694), the generic Greater/Geq ops removed (cb74dcc172, bfd569fcb0) to simplify rules and prepare for integer-in-range checks. Layout: exit blocks are laid out at the end (42d4df9459; blocks post-dominated by exits also treated as cold, “empirically yields better register allocation”), ssa/layout replaced in 1.17 by a depth-first topological sort that removes the primary-predecessor mechanism, adapts loop rotation and changes regalloc’s primary predecessor selection (600259b099). Register allocation: dead-slot clobbering only at calls under clobberdead (c8545722a1, 360771e422, extended 6ae3b70ef2, 9fbcba6664), reuse a dead register before one holding a constant (72dc9ab191), phi register choice considering all predecessors (1c0d1f4e97), desired registers for live values (b2a8317b31), valState slice reuse (4ae31dc8c5), copy deallocation fix (382fe3e249), register reuse on edge state becomes an ICE (48403b268b), “desired only if it satisfies register mask” (5b328c4a2f), 8a317ebc0f, mask fixes. Scheduling: OpArg earlier (9a7e70e34f). The scheduler tie-breaks on Value.Uses before ID (943a0d02d1), more non-ID comparisons (80ced39396). Others: pre-existing ssa.html gets CFGs via dot (3068fcfa0d), GOSSAHASH package-sensitive (4220d67084), shortcircuit for blocks with other phis (ade0811dc8), phiopt types (d889f0cb10), proved bounds remove signed-division fix-ups (13d5cd7847), prove ignoring div/mod on non-x86 (2c859eae1d), NaN constants forbidden in SSA (2aa7c6c548, cd9fd640db), nil check ordering by position (ff9481ec0d), 2c423f063b index info on bounds failure.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: bce1f12225, 13d5cd7847, 3068fcfa0d, ff9481ec0d, 5403b8eceb, f493e55723, a3593685cf. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.13 — Done: 80b6812d7b, 4ae31dc8c5, 8a317ebc0f, 2c423f063b. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.14 — Done: multiple control values (9c2e7e8bed), postorder simplification (75198b9a9c), 72dc9ab191. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: exit layout, Greater/Geq removal, comparison canonicalization, scheduler uses, shortcircuit phis, flagalloc cleanup, d7c073ecbf, 806318d6ad. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: 1c0d1f4e97, b2a8317b31, 91b7619310, bf833ead62, 37a32a1833, 6c64b6db68 (no constant fold of divide by zero), a4b95cd092 (comparison folding fix). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.17 — Done: depth-first layout (600259b099), 6ae3b70ef2, 5b328c4a2f, 90ec257735, b38b1b2f9a, 4357f71ca7. Left open: 600259b099 accepts that some functions get larger or slower.

Safepoints, unsafe points and stack maps for asynchronous preemption

Span: Go 1.14 → Go 1.16 · Status at go1.17: stack maps only at call sites; register maps removed; unsafe-point info in PCDATA → continues as Stack slot merging, liveness and stack maps (1.18+)

Earlier history: Liveness, stack maps, safepoints and write barriers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #24543 runtime: non-cooperative goroutine preemption referenced by 1 of this thread's commits
  • design doc Proposal: Non-cooperative goroutine preemption Austin Clements, 2019-01-18 · linked from #24543
  • tracking issue #36365 runtime: clean up async preemption loose ends referenced by 5 of this thread's commits
  • motivating issue #10958 runtime: tight loops should be preemptible referenced by 1 of this thread's commits

Design. To support signal-based preemption, assemblers and the compiler must say which PCs are not safe points. In 1.14 the compiler marks unsafe points (4a7ed1fab7), architecture-specific marking in obj for arm64 (4736088463), mips (69dcdbd2ba, a96cfa75c6), ppc64 (ceca99bdeb), s390x (4751db93ef), x86 two-instruction TLS access (498eaee461); the encoding moves from stack-map index -2 to register-map index because -2 could not mark CALLs (c3f149250e); split-stack prologues marked nonpreemptible (b2482e4817); a missing initial PCDATA bug (initial value is -1, not -2) is fixed (61fa79885b). In 1.15 9d812cfa5c limits stack maps to call sites and replaces register maps with unsafe-point info, behind go115ReduceLiveness: exe size -5.72%, pclntab -21.08%. Calls in nosplit functions are separated from unsafe-point bits (faafdf5115), 6bf2eea62a fixes StackMapDontCare for unused reg maps, 601bc41da2 drops stack maps for write barrier calls, 2bad2f7eba marks PanicBounds/Extend as calls, ee7d9f1c37 makes LivenessMap sparse, f84bbd52b0 marks block control unsafe. In 1.16 84d7a85089 deletes register maps entirely, DUFFZERO/DUFFCOPY become async unsafe because they stash the frame pointer below SP (01f99b4e95), and deferreturn liveness is fixed (32a84c99e1). Related: c8545722a1 clobberdead experiment limited to calls.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.12 — Done: only call-site clobbering experiment (c8545722a1, 360771e422). Left open: “stack maps at non-call safepoints are still imprecise” (c8545722a1).
  • Go 1.14 — Done: unsafe-point marking across ports; c3f149250e, b2482e4817, 61fa79885b. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.15 — Done: 9d812cfa5c, faafdf5115, 601bc41da2, 2bad2f7eba, ee7d9f1c37. Left open: flag-gated.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: 84d7a85089, 01f99b4e95, 32a84c99e1. Left open: nothing noted.

New object file format and content-addressable symbols (dev.link, assembler side)

Span: Go 1.14 → Go 1.16 · Status at go1.17: done; the linker consumes indexed objects (goobj2) → continues in the linker threads (1.18+)

Earlier history: cmd/internal/obj: Prog/LSym refactoring, concurrent backend and object-writing (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design docs & discussion
  • design doc (PUBLIC) Building a better Go linker listed in Go: A Documentary

Design. The assembler and cmd/internal/obj write object files in a new format that references symbols by (package index, symbol index) instead of names. 2c484c0356 adds the writer, with cmd/internal/goobj2 created; indices are assigned in compiler/asm and propagated in export data (53b7c18284); d56c8149ac uses index for static symbols; 97e497b253 references by name when linking against shared libraries. The old format is the default in 1.14 (9cf6c65ca3), the new reenabled by default in 1.15 (8cdb769b08), old support deleted from compiler/asm (181faef82c) and entirely (c89251204e). Fingerprints guard index consistency (e08f10b8b5, hash of export data 7795523910). Content-addressable symbols identified by hashes: pseudo-package PkgIdxHashed (27342e5bd9), short hash (4f217d5aaa), applied to GC maps (17344d55d6), constants (3c54069907), read-only static temps (289c238a33), type names (66770f4b1d), with relocations (526d99a49a), trailing-zero trim (b3e3c339ff), length (b249703e3c), Hashed64 size (2ad44158af). Others: DWARF sub-symbols as aux (8634642f9a, ad92148058, 673a02a235, 62b0790a79), LSym.Func moved into Extra (912262b806), FuncID computed in compiler (89cf569a45), per-package filenames (9bdaf99966), -p package path written at compile time (cc5eaf9346, saving ~100MB allocations in the linker), AttrSeenGlobl removed (c2e73fb446), deterministic file order (991adcd21b), large functions aligned (d92a5a80b5).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.14 — Done: 2c484c0356, 53b7c18284, cd75cf4bc0, d56c8149ac, 97e497b253, 9cf6c65ca3, ffca64dcf3. Left open: “currently nothing will consume the new object file” (2c484c0356).
  • Go 1.15 — Done: 8cdb769b08, 181faef82c, 330f53b615, 6c7d6cefd0, 88d6d37b77, e08f10b8b5, f5fcc9b8e0. Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.16 — Done: content-addressable symbols and cleanup (hashes above), c89251204e. Left open: type descriptors are not yet dedup’d (526d99a49a says deduplication is “just an optimization, not a requirement … until we get to type descriptors”).

Assembler directives and tooling: PCALIGN/ALIGN, FuncInfo flags, prologue handling

ADJSP pcsp fix (9d032026d6). Huge-frame prologue simplification across x86, arm, arm64, mips, ppc64, riscv, s390x (ef3122e909, 24dd8cfe23, 4702dd67a7, 2b63404ddb, a06b08e7d1, 042f4cbb6f, 191167c2b2), x86 TLS offset (68c664141c), cmd/asm rejects code that uses a clobbered R15 under dynamic linking (c870e86329), refined buildcfg move (95ed5c3800), cmd/asm object header (cef3a442ea), Prog.SetFrom3{Reg,Const} (a61524d103), obj IsAsm flag (f5fcc9b8e0), branch target recording simplification (8247da3662, 9e70564f63), -S consistency (75fab04b83).

Register-based calling convention (ABIInternal) ports beyond amd64

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.26 · Status at HEAD: register ABI enabled on amd64, arm64, ppc64x, riscv64, loong64, s390x; 386, arm and mips* still stack-based

Earlier history: Per-architecture compilers 6g/8g/5g/9g and the shared gc code generator (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · Register-based ABI (ABIInternal) and ABI wrappers (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17) · Late call expansion, AuxCall and the expand_calls pass (Go 1.16 → Go 1.17)

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #40724 cmd/compile: switch to a register-based calling convention for Go functions referenced by 16 of this thread's commits
  • design doc Proposal: Register-based Go calling convention Austin Clements, 2020-08-10 · linked from #40724

Design. The register ABI (ABIInternal) assigns integer/FP arguments and results to fixed register sequences described per architecture in cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen/*Ops.go plus cmd/compile/internal/abi (ABIConfig, abiutils). Enabling it on an architecture needs a fixed recipe, visible in every port: (1) define parameter registers and make sure no other fixed-purpose register (closure context register, duff-device temporaries, REGTMP) overlaps them; (2) update the CALL* ops (CALLstatic/CALLclosure/CALLinter) so arguments are register inputs; (3) add “initial spill support” — arg/result load/spill code (ssagen‘s LoadRegResult/spillArgReg), because each arg has a dedicated spill slot in the caller’s frame; (4) make morestack prologue spill/unspill the argument registers (cmd/internal/obj/<arch> sets MorestackArgs / “regabi prologue”); (5) add the arch to buildcfg and the tests’ hasRegisterABI. On amd64 the ABI relies on a dedicated G register and a zeroed X15; on other architectures the G register already existed.

Several ABI-adjacent mechanisms were built along the way: argument-stack-slot liveness (so tracebacks mark possibly-stale register-passed args with ?), clobberdead debugging mode per arch, wrappers using tail calls (OTAILCALL now wraps a real OCALL so args can be placed by SSA), and maymorestack hooks.

Register allocator, scheduler and block-level backend passes

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: ongoing tuning each cycle

Earlier history: Register allocation and the peephole optimizer (reg.c, peep.c) (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · SSA backend bring-up on amd64 (dev.ssa merge) (Go 1.7 → Go 1.7) · Register allocation, flag allocation and stack slots (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Scheduling, tighten, block layout and CFG passes (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · DWARF variable locations, statement positions and inline info from the backend (Go 1.9 → Go 1.11) · SSA infrastructure passes: layout, regalloc, scheduling, flagalloc, block shape (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design. regalloc.go is a linear-scan-style allocator over blocks in a visit order: each block starts from a chosen predecessor’s endRegs, values get registers using per-value “desired” registers (computeDesired), and a final shuffle pass reconciles each edge. Over the period, work concentrated on (a) giving ops richer register constraints, (b) cheaper/better liveness, (c) smarter spill/rematerialization, and (d) a forward scheduler with arch-specific score tweaks. Scheduling (schedule.go) was converted from backward to forward scheduling so values can be placed as soon as they are ready; scores (ScoreReadFlags, ScoreCarryChainTail, ScoreMemory, …) control flag and carry-chain adjacency.

amd64 code generation and GOAMD64 microarchitecture levels

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: GOAMD64=v1 default; v3 unlocks BMI1/BMI2/LZCNT/MOVBE/FMA codegen; constant churn of peephole rules

Earlier history: Per-architecture compilers 6g/8g/5g/9g and the shared gc code generator (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · Expression and statement code quality in 6g/8g/5g (division, bounds checks, loops, slices, interfaces) (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · amd64 and 386 instruction selection (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · x86 assembler: AVX, AVX2, AVX-512 and the instruction table (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · amd64 lowering: read-modify-write, load-op, addressing modes pass, intrinsic-friendly rules (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #45453 all: add GOAMD64 environment variable referenced by 3 of this thread's commits

Design. GOAMD64=v1..v4 is checked at compile time through buildcfg.GOAMD64 (ssa.Config), and v1 builds are guarded by a test (TestGoAMD64v1) that disassembles to ensure no >v1 instruction slips in (cbd7200167, 5d946f1892, bb1749ba3b, more robust v1 detection 515040548c). Where an instruction is only legal at v3, rules gate on it. The code generator is rules in AMD64.rules/AMD64latelower.rules plus the amd64/ssa.go emitter; the late-lower pass (below) was introduced for AMD64 LEA/shift patterns.

arm64 code generation and assembler

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: active; assembler gaining a table-driven SVE/ASIMD path; SVE under GOEXPERIMENT=simd

Earlier history: Assemblers: 5a/6a/8a/9a and the Go cmd/asm (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · The arm64 (ARMv8) port (7g/7a/7l) (Go 1.5 → Go 1.6) · Multi-architecture SSA ports: ARM, 386, ARM64 (dev.ssa) (Go 1.7 → Go 1.8) · ARM and ARM64 instruction selection and fused operations (Go 1.8 → Go 1.11) · ARM64 assembler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · arm64 backend and assembler (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design docs & discussion
  • tracking issue #44734 cmd/asm: refactor the framework of the arm64 assembler referenced by 2 of this thread's commits
  • discussion x86 asm source of truth golang-dev · linked from #44734

Design. Compiler side: ARM64.rules/ARM64latelower.rules with bitfield (UBFX/SBFIZ/BFI), CMP/CMN/TST, CSEL/CSET, conditional-compare, rotate and shifted-operand forms. Assembler side (cmd/internal/obj/arm64): optab classes with a literal pool, REGTMP (R27) use for synthesized sequences, span7 passes, prologue/epilogue emission in obj7.go. In 1.27 a second, data-driven assembling path was added: generated instruction tables (anames_gen.go, encoding_gen.go, goops_gen.go, inst_gen.go) entered through tryEncode, designed for SVE and newer ASIMD forms.

riscv64 compiler and assembler (RVA profiles, vector, compressed)

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: GORISCV64 rva20u64/rva22u64/rva23u64 profiles drive Zba/Zbb/Zbs/Zicond codegen; assembler supports V, crypto vector suites and compressed (RVC) emission

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #71105 cmd/compile: change GORISCV64=rva20u64 to include compressed instructions referenced by 7 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #61476 all: add GORISCV64 environment variable linked from #71105

Design. The compiler lowers to RV64G with sequences for shifts (go semantics: shift counts ≥64 give 0 or sign), then peephole-folds immediates and sign extensions in RISCV64.rules. The assembler (obj/riscv) originally rewrote obj.Prog into pseudo-expansions; 1.18 reworked it to avoid Prog rewriting and generate machine code directly from instructionsForMOV etc. A generated instruction table (inst.go, regenerated from the spec; make driven in 1.27 d484fb9ddf) holds encodings. GORISCV64 selects profiles (rva20u64 / rva22u64 / rva23u64): at rva22u64+ the compiler may emit Zba/Zbb/Zbs instructions without runtime checks, and at rva20u64 it emits a Zbb runtime check only where profitable (OnesCount).

loong64 backend and assembler

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: feature-complete port with LSX/LASX assembler coverage; very active

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #46229 all: port to linux/loong64 referenced by 8 of this thread's commits

Design. loong64 was added as an architecture in 1.18 (c7f09eeb13), then given SSA rules/ops (ec5bdefd0a, 756fcd8fc2, 2136e15510, a2d12076b9), assembler registers/instructions (c1105cfd43) and tests (335569b598, 0653cb4cf7) in 1.19. PPC64 / Power10 backend (GOPPC64, prefixed instructions, PC-relative code)

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: power8/9/10 levels; PC-relative (NOTOC) code on power10/linux

Earlier history: The ppc64 / ppc64le port (dev.power64, 9g/9a/9l) (Go 1.5 → Go 1.6) · Multi-architecture SSA ports: PPC64, MIPS64, MIPS32, s390x (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · 32-bit ARM, MIPS and PPC64 assemblers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · PPC64 / POWER backend and assembler (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design docs & discussion
  • tracking issue #44549 cmd/asm,cmd/compile,cmd/link,cmd/objdump: ppc64 ISA 3.1 support referenced by 4 of this thread's commits

Design. GOPPC64=power8|power9|power10 gates instruction selection. Power10 adds prefixed loads/stores/addi with 34-bit displacements and PC-relative addressing; the assembler selects them by dynamically configuring optab (72301a9863), emitting new always-PC-relative relocations. Because such code needs no TOC pointer, the compiler/assembler/linker stop maintaining R2 on linux/ppc64 with power10, shrinking PIC binaries ~2% (k8s binaries −1.8…−2.5%) (29d5272da8, linker PCrel ccb8db88c5). The assembler grew carry/XER modelling so bits.Add64/Sub64 lower into SSA with CA tracking.

Duff’s device replaced by generated loops; Zero/Move lowering

Span: Go 1.20 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: done for amd64, arm64, loong64, riscv64; runtime duff code removed for arm64, loong64, riscv64

Earlier history: Zeroing and copying: Duff’s device, REP, unaligned moves and AVX2 runtime assembly (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · Memory clearing and copying: Zero, Move and Duff’s device (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. LoweredZero/LoweredMove (and …Loop) ops emit inline instruction sequences and a counted loop instead of jumping into the runtime’s hand-unrolled duffzero/duffcopy. Unrolled Duff code needed special registers, nil-check handling and could not be traced well. Generated loops pick unroll size by length, avoid DUFF* registers constraint, simplify zerorange (in ggen), and let the register allocator choose registers. Ops like LoweredMemmoveLoop use wider vector ops (NEON/LSX) where available.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.25 — Done: nil check done before calling duff functions on arm64/amd64 dbaa2d3e65; noDuffDevice flag removed 26040b1dd7.
  • Go 1.26 — Done: amd64: DUFFZERO and DUFFCOPY replaced by generated loops (eb7f515c4d,ec9e1176c3; the DUFFCOPY change was reverted 4e182db5fc and relanded ca66f907dd); arm64 (28aa529c99,15d6dbc05c) with runtime duff removed e4291e484c; riscv64 and loong64 (879ff736d3,4dac9e093f,7bba745820,91e76a513b) with runtime duff removed (b9a4a09b0f,4f7bbc62c7); zerorange simplified on amd64/arm64/riscv64/loong64/mips/mips64 (b10eb1d042,5e94d72158,77643dc63f,e0870a0a12,06e791c0cd,bb48272e24; mips fix 0b26678db2); zero constant register reuse on mips64x bdd51e7855.

Bounds-check calls: new “panicBounds” strategy

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.26 · Status at HEAD: all architectures converted; old style removed

Design. Instead of loading index/length into fixed argument registers and calling panicIndex variants, the failing bounds-check emits a single call instruction whose operands are the registers that already hold index and length, plus a pcdata table so the runtime can recover them (static analysis in the cmd/go sample: 6877 of ~7650 checks are just the call itself; only 139 need a reg-reg move, 602 a constant load). Reduces cmd/go text ~0.8%, total binary ~0.2% after the new pcdata table.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: per-arch migration: arm64 394d0bee8d, amd64/386 076eae436e, arm32 7dccd6395c, loong64 5216fd570e, mips64 9f9d7b50e8, mips32 8330fb48a6, riscv64 95693816a5, s390x 7a1679d7ae, ppc64 802d056c78; old-style calls removed 21ab0128b6; bounds-check slice SUB/SUBconst compare optimization dcb479c2f9, shift-through-AND folding for slices bd80f74bc1; bounds report fix af03343f93; ppc64 panicBounds frame made smaller e0a1ea431c. Left open: nothing noted.

Late-lower pass, memory-op combining and arch-independent rule migration

Span: Go 1.20 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: late lower on amd64, arm64, ppc64, riscv64; memcombine arch-independent

Earlier history: Rewrite-rule machinery and compile-time performance of the SSA compiler (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Memory-op combining, byte-order idioms and load/store folding (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11)

Design. The “lower” pass has no ordering among rules; lateLower is a second round of lowering that runs rules which must fire last (e.g., split constant folding that would materialize a constant repeatedly, or turn 3-operand LEA into simpler forms) ddc7d2a80c, with a “late lower block” function c0f27eb3d5. Memory op combining was removed from arch rules into one arch-independent pass memcombine (cedf5008a8: removed ~900 lines from ARM64.rules, ~490 from AMD64.rules; handles out-of-order writes), later extended to loads that feed stores e713d6f939 and store order/line number fixes 657c885fb9. Rotate detection moved to generic rules 60ad3c48f5; canRotate per arch.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.21 — Done: memcombine pass cedf5008a8; generic rules cleanup: store rules use store type 60140a86b3.

Stack slot merging, liveness and stack maps

Span: Go 1.23 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: merge-locals on by default; analysis tightened in 1.28

Earlier history: Stack frames, pointer maps and liveness analysis in the compiler (Go 1.2 → Go 1.6) · Liveness, stack maps, safepoints and write barriers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Safepoints, unsafe points and stack maps for asynchronous preemption (Go 1.14 → Go 1.16)

Design docs & discussion
  • motivating issue #62737 cmd/compile: merge temporaries and named variables by GC shape referenced by 4 of this thread's commits

Design. cmd/compile/internal/liveness gained a “live intervals” utility (7979c8f588) and a mergelocals pass that overlaps stack slots of disjointly live locals (e01b1eb289: now allows B smaller than A, non-pointer merged into pointer slot; candidates sorted by pointerness, alignment, size, name; GC shape no longer compared since two vars sharing a slot are never both live across a call; total saved bytes on sweet rose from 91,256 to 124,336). Addr-taken candidates are handled when only the arch memory op’s SymAddr touches the var 82e929e4f8. SIMD vars excluded 1440ff7036. Related liveness/stackmap pieces: argument-slot liveness (see ABI thread), ArgInfo/ArgsPointerMaps implicit setup for asm functions 208f361800, args_stackmap for ABI0 assembly functions regardless of linkname 0b72631a82, GOSSAFUNC liveness output 7472b4c324, sorted liveness reports 4ff074945a.

Prologue, frame pointer, stack split and function alignment (cmd/internal/obj)

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: per-arch; amd64 uses PUSH/POP BP and LEAVE

Earlier history: Stack frame layout, prologues, stack split and frame pointers (Go 1.0 → Go 1.6) · liblink: a shared assembler/linker library (Go 1.3 → Go 1.5) · Normalising Prog/Addr in cmd/internal/obj (the portable instruction representation) (Go 1.5 → Go 1.6) · Position-independent code, dynamic linking and TLS in the assemblers (Go 1.3 → Go 1.6) · Removal of the legacy backend and decoupling gc from the code generators (Go 1.7 → Go 1.9) · cmd/internal/obj: Prog/LSym refactoring, concurrent backend and object-writing (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Prologues, frame pointers, NOFRAME and tail calls (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · Assembler directives and tooling: PCALIGN/ALIGN, FuncInfo flags, prologue handling (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design. Each obj/<arch>/obj*.go preprocess emits stack-split checks, frame setup and return sequences. Changes are about shrinking the sequence, avoiding writes below SP before the frame exists (signal safety), and making branch layout favour the common path: arm64 STP/LDP and single-instruction LR+SP save for small frames; amd64 PUSH BP/POP BP or LEAVE; mips/s390x/riscv/loong64 save LR after decrementing SP (3562977b6f, 3ed8a1e629); loong64 inverts stacksplit branch (5923a97f43,9350068b23). PCALIGN was extended to amd64/386 and PCALIGNMAX added. Frameless detection became explicit (NOFRAME) rather than heuristic on amd64.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.19 — Done: arm64 c6d9b38dd8,64ef16e777,31be6285a8; 3562977b6f (mips, s390x, riscv).
  • Go 1.21 — Done: amd64 BP save via PUSH/POP f66581ead6, explicit NOFRAME on every OS + removal of heuristic (d939b3717f…d20e688fcf).
  • Go 1.22 — Done: PCALIGN on 386/amd64 f322d67ced.

Multi-word arithmetic, intrinsics and carry-chain support

Span: Go 1.18 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: Add64/Sub64/Mul64 intrinsics on all 64-bit ports; 32-bit support for Mul64 added in 1.26

Earlier history: Intrinsics for atomics, math/bits, math and runtime helpers (Go 1.7 → Go 1.11) · math/bits, atomic and runtime intrinsics (cross-architecture) (Go 1.12 → Go 1.17)

Design. math/bits intrinsics lower to flag/carry-aware SSA ops. Architectures with a carry bit in a flag/special register (PPC64 XER.CA, arm64 flags) need the scheduler to keep carry chains contiguous: a carry-using op group is scored below other ops and carry-generating ops later so only one chain is in flight (c386269ed8), with ScoreCarryChainTail ordered before ScoreMemory but after ScoreReadFlags on arm64 (669ec549b5).
