Compiler SIMD type system, ABI and register-allocation support

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: SIMD types, vec/mask register classes, ABI passing, X15 zeroing, CPU-feature-aware block analysis and VEX encodings exist on master behind GOEXPERIMENT=simd (X15 whole-register zeroing is unconditional); RegMask widened beyond 64 bits for SVE predicates.

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #73787 simd/archsimd: architecture-specific SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #79781
  • proposal #78902 simd: architecture and vector-size agnostic SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #79781

Design. SIMD vectors are ordinary Go structs in the library (type Float32x4 struct { float32x4 v128; vals [4]float32 }, in src/simd/archsimd/types_amd64.go), but the first field is a tag type (v128/v256/v512, each containing an uncomparable [0]func() so vectors are not ==-comparable, 5a78e1a4a1). The compiler’s types package recognises the tag (typeIsSIMDTag) and marks every type containing it typeIsSIMD; simdify assigns size, alignment and register counts. SSA has dedicated types TypeVec128/256/512 and TypeMask (width 8; the comment notes spilling a mask “will be interesting”), so a value is either a vector-register class value or a mask-register class value. IsSIMD() is then consulted by abi/abiutils.go (SIMD params and results are register-assigned like floats, one register per vector), ssagen/abi.go, liveness/plive.go, amd64/ssa.go (simdReg, simdOrMaskReg, simdRegBySize choose X/Y/Z register names by value size) and the inliner.

Machine ops are described to regalloc by generated “register shapes” in ssa/_gen/AMD64Ops.go / simdAMD64ops.go: the shape names (v11, v21, v2k, kv, v2kv, v31, vgpv, …) say how many vector (v), mask (k), gp and fp inputs/outputs an instruction has. Many were added one by one as new instruction classes appeared (fp1m1fp1 for load-op forms 1161228bf1, fp3fp1 6bc3505773, fp3m1fp1 884f646966, fp1gp1fp1 1b87d52549, with a naming cleanup e32488003d/5429328b0c, and removal of fused-op shapes 1313521f75). Masked “merging” ops are resultInArg0 so the destination register doubles as the merge source (86b4fe31d9).

Because AVX2/AVX-512 are not guaranteed on amd64, the compiler runs a cpufeatures pass over SSA blocks (d2270bccbd, ba72ee0f30): it tracks which CPU features are in scope in each block (reached only through a feature check, signature mentions an AVX type, or the block contains an instruction needing one) and records the maximum feature per function. Later consumers: SIMD-typed zero values are placed so as not to leak features (d61b240b11 puts SIMD zeros in the right block since they may need guarding by a feature check; fbea197d32 stops no-code values such as SIMD zeros from implying features, because the map fast path under GOEXPERIMENT=simd was claiming AVX in every block), critical-edge split blocks inherit the features of their edge (0b2fd4aa9c), and spills/moves/copies/Zero/Move use VEX encodings when AVX is proven present to avoid AVX-SSE transition penalties (5763a306d2, c2f76b656d; issue case: variable shifts ~65x slower due to a legacy MOVQ). An attempt to seed entry features from GOAMD64=v3/v4 (bc769ea44b) was reverted because it broke simd builders (4a1a9dfeb7).

X15 is the ABIInternal zero register. Originally only its low 128 bits were zeroed on function entry (f38e968aba: zeroing the upper part makes the CPU consider it “dirty” and slow SSE code; 256/512-bit zeros are built on the fly); later the whole X/Y/Z15 is zeroed on entry, unconditionally, with a note that earlier attempts (CL 698237) were suspected of regressions but the new benchmarks show none (3f1287d96a). Inlining budget gets a multiplier for functions with SIMD parameters/closures because abstractions over vectors otherwise lose to the cost model (simdCreditMultiplier in inline/inl.go; bumped again for rotate emulation in d7b3da6e25). For arm64 SVE, the register set bitmask RegisterSet (one bit per register in a uint64) silently dropped registers >=64 such as P1-P15, so it was widened to ssaop.RegMask (966c78ed74); ppc64 got F31/vector registers in its regMask in preparation for SIMD there (d934b909f6).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: register shapes, vec/mask SSA types and the first AMD64 SIMD lowering (8ecbd59ebb generated 63k lines: simdssa.go, simdAMD64.rules, simdAMD64ops.go, simdgenericOps.go, simdintrinsics.go); helpers moved from generated code into the compiler (6c50c8b892); vectors made uncomparable (5a78e1a4a1); CPU-feature pass (d2270bccbd, ba72ee0f30); X15 low-128 zeroing (f38e968aba). Left open: spilling masks (“will depend on the architecture”), 256/512-bit zero values built on the fly, VZEROUPPER not evaluated (f38e968aba).
  • Go 1.27 — Done: isSIMD plumbing reused unchanged for WASM (obj.WasmV128 in ssagen/abi.go) and arm64 NEON (8a1b0c8ecb); unsigned-constant fix for load folding (3f6eabdf091.26 was 1.26) ; cgocallback X15 clearing fixes by runtime team (52fd498a96, cross-area). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.28 — Done: SIMD-zero block placement (d61b240b11), no-code values not implying features (fbea197d32), VEX encodings (5763a306d2), critical-edge features (0b2fd4aa9c), whole-X15 zeroing (3f1287d96a), RegMask widening (966c78ed74), GOAMD64 seeding attempted and reverted (bc769ea44b, 4a1a9dfeb7). Left open: GOAMD64-derived feature seeding.

simdgen: the instruction-table-driven generator

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: lives in src/simd/archsimd/_gen (separate module) with simdgen, unify, tmplgen, wasmgen, midway, specgen, gentools; one go generate regenerates everything.

Design docs & discussion
  • tracking issue #81819 simd: unify API generation around executable spec referenced by 1 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #78902 simd: architecture and vector-size agnostic SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #81819

Design. Almost all of src/simd/archsimd/ops_*.go, the compiler’s simdAMD64.rules, simdAMD64ops.go, simdgenericOps.go, ssagen/simd*intrinsics.go, amd64/simdssa.go and (for the other targets) their ARM64/Wasm analogues are generated. simdgen reads Intel XED instruction data (xeddata; fetch-xed.sh), unifies it with hand-written YAML (go_amd64.yaml, types.yaml, categories.yaml) using a constraint-style unify package (values with environments; unify.Value.Decode, bijective field-name canonicalisation a5ed3e905c), and emits Go declarations with doc comments, generic SSA ops, machine ops, rewrite rules and intrinsic registrations. The machine-op generator knows op shapes (the v11... register classes), whether an op is resultInArg0, commutative, has an immediate, has memory forms, and its required CPU feature; features carry an implication table so AVX512 implies AVX2 etc. (9ef1692c93), a feature check API is generated per CPU feature (934dbcea1a) and AVXAES is exposed as a single combined check.

The generator was originally in golang.org/x/arch/internal/simdgen, and commits had to be paired between repos (“PAIRED w/ arch/internal/simdgen CL 681615”, 6c50c8b892; 0870ed04a3 “generated by CL 686215”). It was migrated into the main repo as simd/_gen in 1.26 (b7c8698549) because coordinating x/arch commits with the generated files caused “tremendous process friction”; the migration commit is itself script-generated and builds a self-contained module. Test generation moved from simdgen to the Go repo using generics (88568519b4, *_helpers_test.go generated), and template code generation moved into _gen with go generate generating everything (cf45adf140, 3fe246ae0f); generate.go has a goexperiment tag so that the package does not exist when the experiment is off (61a5a6b016).

In 1.27 simdgen was generalised from amd64 to a per-architecture parametrisation: templates for intrinsics, SSA ops, rules and types take the target (8a1b0c8ecb), an ARM64 ISA XML parser feeds NEON (8437d1b188), YAML configs were reorganised by architecture (951257bd14), the rule-generation template and intrinsic definition were refactored (0442e04934, 593e8bf9b1), output ordering made deterministic (dfd75f82d4, e3afca43e2, b93d81957e), and a tmplgen produces typed test helpers (61a10105e6). In 1.28 common code moved into gentools (GOROOT discovery robust to a broken tree, post-processing hook, 7d634c347a..fe5d9816fd, f619436443, 98283d7ebf), the external data dependencies were redone (babec569e7), SSA generic ops are written separately (6b5417f030), and the tool works with any Go toolchain >= 1.26 (6ddf3bfac0). AGENTS.md/README guidance for tool users appeared (fd36608473, c3cbcf4169).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: first generated amd64 code (8ecbd59ebb); generator output ordering fixes (3a4d10bfca removed a map iteration, 35b8cf7fed, e62e377ed6); simdgen migrated into the repo (b7c8698549) with etetest.sh rewrite (8b90d48d8c); tests generated in repo (88568519b4, a24ffe3379); memory operand parsing and merge (f42c9261d3, 0b323350a5, 5a0446d449); SHA features parsed from XED (2b8eded4f4); feature implications (9ef1692c93). Left open: the generator depends on XED data path ($XEDDATA); the API source of truth is spread over YAML categories, hand-written files and docs.
  • Go 1.27 — Done: multi-architecture parametrisation and ARM64 definitions (8a1b0c8ecb, 8437d1b188, 951257bd14); asmRule for patterns on asm instructions (9922fb1d24); argsMatchRule for broadcast-to-VMOVI folding (098d688071); ImmMax to limit immediate jump-table sizes (b84139dfad); SetElem general-register width detection (f4d50e5ebf); auto-merge of simdgenericOps.go (d3a3061d75); zero-valued fields omitted from simdAMD64ops.go (6fb7a1cddd); decode non-broadcast memory operands (4136ffed69); insert_ordered_map for deterministic output (82489f7402). Left open: sort-order glitch only “attempted to pin down” (e3afca43e2).
  • Go 1.28 — Done: gentools consolidation, Operand type filled by XED/ARM64/SVE (7b916597d3, 1f0d9ab3af), README, GOROOT logic; “mem” naming (c5612f0ccf); CPU feature of mask ops (f507c3fc9f). Left open: transition of old inputs (categories.yaml) to the executable spec, see spec thread.

AMD64 archsimd API: AVX, AVX2 and AVX-512 operations

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: simd/archsimd provides 128/256/512-bit vectors on amd64 with operations that map to AVX/AVX2/AVX-512 instructions; experimental (GOEXPERIMENT=simd), not under Go 1 compatibility.

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #73787 simd/archsimd: architecture-specific SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #76473
  • proposal #78979 proposal: simd/archsimd: enable AMD64 architecture-specific SIMD by default referenced by 3 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #76473 simd: rename low-level SIMD package to simd/archsimd (GOEXPERIMENT) referenced by 1 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #78902 simd: architecture and vector-size agnostic SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #78979

Design. Vector types are Int8x16 … Float64x8; each operation is a method (func (x Int32x4) Add(y Int32x4) Int32x4), declared without a body and implemented as a compiler intrinsic; its doc comment names the assembler op and CPU feature (“Asm: VPADDD, CPU Feature: AVX”). The API deliberately does not expose every instruction: “the compiler recognizes certain patterns … and may optimize them to more performant instructions” (e.g. Add followed by Masked becomes a masked AVX-512 add). The surface was built in waves of generated families: arithmetic, comparisons, rounding (34a9cdef87), dot products and fused multiply-add (9ba7db36b5, ded6e0ac71, ca01eab9c7), shifts and rotates (e61ebfce56, 82d056ddd7), Galois-field ops (10c9621936), insert/extract (1fa4bcfcda, 7fadfa9638, 292db9b676, 43a61aef56), permutes and Compress/Expand (01f7f57025, 6d10680141, 5b0ef7fcdc), blend (7ca34599ec), Broadcast (ddb689c7bb), Get/SetLo/Hi (d3cf582f8a), interleave and VSHUFP (b509516b2e, bf00f5dfd6), select-from-pair (25c36b95d1, ea3b2ecd28), integer conversions of every width/saturation flavour (4fce49b86c, f4c41d9922, 7fdb1da6b0, 4fa23b0d29, bc217d4170) plus float<->int (86cd9b5c90, d6564ed088, f3a306527c), VPSADBW, VPLZCNT, AES, SHA, VPTERNLOG, VPALIGNR and carryless multiply (703a5fbaad, cf7c1a4cbb, d03634f807, 95871e4a00, 3417b48b17).

Design decisions visible in the history: FP comparisons involving NaN return false (immediates for Equal/Greater/GreaterEqual changed, 0870ed04a3); FP bitwise logic ops removed from the API (56ca67682b) and bitwise ops made available for all integer vectors (3f92aa1eca); Masked$OP renamed $(OP)Masked (029d7ec3e9); PairDotProdAccumulate->AddDotProd->DotProduct (c2d775d401, 416332dba2); a “best instruction” choice for compare-by-immediate that respects commutativity (608dba4308); IsNaN made unary and renamed (13440fb518; compiles to VCMPPS $3, x, x); String() methods (c75965b666); 128/256-bit FMA no longer needs AVX-512 (e242961960); DotProductQuadruple deleted for now (70c22e0ad7). Fast transposes were demonstrated as a performance example (1c961c2fb2; tiled 8x8 transpose ~4.7x faster than plain on the 88-core Xeon in that message).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: user-visible the whole API above reached master through reverse merges starting d4f5650cc5 (2025-11-24), 2b62144069 (12-03), 9e09812308 (12-08); package renamed simd -> simd/archsimd with package doc (144cf17d2c, 1da0c29c2a); doc rewrites (05e41225f6..d64add4d60), Mask.AsIntMxN->ToIntMxN and ToMask only on integer vectors (f110ba540c, c0ba519764); Broadcast rename (8ac4477d83); tests skipped without AVX (1b291b70df). Left open: many names still to rename (see API shaping thread); DotProductQuadruple removed pending redesign (70c22e0ad7).

Left open: nothing noted.

Mask representation, masked operations and merge peepholes

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: masks are opaque MaskNxM types in archsimd; amd64 uses K registers where AVX-512 is available and vector registers otherwise; arm64 SVE uses predicate registers; IfElse/Masked replace Merge.

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #73787 simd/archsimd: architecture-specific SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #78979

Design. A mask has an opaque type (Mask8x16 struct with ToBits() uint16, Mask8x16FromBits). In the compiler a mask is TypeMask in the mask register class for AVX-512 (K registers) and an ordinary vector-sized value for AVX/AVX2 compare results. Semantics: converting a vector to a mask sets an element true iff the vector element is nonzero (a034826e26, ToMask, with asMask unexported); mask->vector yields all-ones/zero lanes. Comparisons produce masks (aab8b173a9, 47b07a87a6 fixed Int64x2 Greater to return a mask type). Rather than expose one API per AVX-512 masked instruction variant, the API exposes plain ops plus Masked / Merge (later IfElse) and the compiler pattern-matches: x.Op(y).Masked(m) -> OpMasked machine op (first sample ede64cf0d8, then many ops cf31b15635, 0f660d675f making OpMasked machine-ops only, and for 128/256-bit “under feature check” 771a1dc216, also fixing masked-load variants to be zeroing by default); x.Op(y).Merge(z, mask) -> OpMasked(z, x, y, mask) where the machine op is resultInArg0 (86b4fe31d9). BLEND instructions are marked “not-zero-mask” (8ccd6c2034). Masked loads/stores were first an API (acc1492b7d, AVX2 VMASKMOV; K-mask slice loads c25e5c86b2), but the API was removed (2e71cf1a2a: “mask load and stores could just be hidden behind peepholes”) and replaced by the LoadTPart / StorePart slice helpers that use them internally (2eaa5a0703, 761894d4a5, b70242b3b9, ec5b41b314).

To support AVX2-only machines, emulations for mask/merge methods were added (94d72355f6) and later “amd64 supports IfElse, not Merge”, with the old methods deprecated using go-fix-inline annotations (e115b2f987); Merge was then removed for 1.27 (6f010acf75). Mask <-> bits conversions (6f7a1164e7, f39711a03d) exist because mask load/store of the register were dropped. Mask bitwise logic on amd64 rewrites to K-register ops when AVX-512 is known (e.g. KANDN, see e2889b0bf5).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: user-visible mask types and conversions (a034826e26, 6f7a1164e7), .Masked() peepholes (ede64cf0d8, cf31b15635), merging ops (86b4fe31d9), emulations of mask/merge methods for AVX2 (94d72355f6, 2080415aa2), mask load/store removal (2e71cf1a2a), ToMask integer-only (f110ba540c). Left open: IfElse naming, Merge emulation wrongly named at first (“under a wrong name; subsequent CLs will … rename”, 94d72355f6).
  • Go 1.27 — Done: user-visible IfElse supersedes Merge (e115b2f987, 6f010acf75), ARM64 IfElse semantics corrected (a2b3c73f75), Mask.ToIntNs repairs (54719fce02), arm64 uint->mask conversions removed because “everyone has signed” (07664b7a53). Left open: nothing noted.
  • Go 1.28 — Done: user-visible mask queries All/Any/None/TrailingZeros, Mask Xor/AndNot/Equal/Not (see AMD64 thread); SVE predicate masks (see SVE thread). Left open: nothing noted.

Memory operands, constant-immediate forms and jump tables

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.27 · Status at HEAD: generated load-op and constant-load rules for AVX/AVX-512; broadcast and non-broadcast memory operands decoded from XED.

Design. Instructions with an immediate (VPSHUFD $imm, shifts, VPEXTR, rounding) take the immediate as a “constant” parameter in the API (4993a91ae1 renamed imm to constant). When the argument is a compile-time constant it is encoded directly; when it is not, the compiler emits a jump table over all 256 values (38b76bf2a3, initial exhaustive, bounds-checked version to follow; wasm uses a binary-search switch expansion with retpoline fixes, 8742584113; b84139dfad adds ImmMax to limit table size). Memory forms: simdgen parses and merges memory operands (f42c9261d3, 0b323350a5), adds machine ops with prog writing (5a0446d449, which also fixed a XED merge bug where features were not checked), memop peepholes x.Op(load) -> op-with-memory (48f366d826), load+const-imm8 variants (3ec0b25ab7, 4eb5c6e07b), rewrite rules consistent on CPU features (443b7aeddb) and memory peepholes where the load’s feature level differs (c4fbf3b4cf). Later decoding was extended to non-broadcast memory operands (4136ffed69, fixes #78159), unsigned constants when folding (3f6eabdf09), and broadcast-to-VMOVI folding (098d688071).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: 38b76bf2a3, 5a0446d449, 48f366d826, 3ec0b25ab7, 4eb5c6e07b, 443b7aeddb, c4fbf3b4cf, 3f6eabdf09. Left open: bounds-checked jump table “in the next CL” (38b76bf2a3).
  • Go 1.27 — Done: 4136ffed69, 098d688071, aa80d7a7e6, b84139dfad. Left open: nothing noted.

dev.simd branch, GOEXPERIMENT=simd lifecycle and merges to master

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: GOEXPERIMENT=simd exists in internal/goexperiment/flags.go, off by default in buildcfg; dev.simd reverse-merged to master repeatedly (development continues “only on dev.simd” and merges “when necessary”).

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #76473 simd: rename low-level SIMD package to simd/archsimd (GOEXPERIMENT) referenced by 1 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #73787 simd/archsimd: architecture-specific SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #76473

Design. All development happened on the dev.simd branch, periodically merged from master. The experiment flag guards the simd and simd/archsimd packages (build tag goexperiment.simd) and the compiler’s SIMD intrinsics. It was introduced as an off-by-default flag (4d2c71ebf9, 2025-05-22) then turned on by default for amd64 on the branch only so developers get it (2ef7106881); before each merge to master the default is turned off (“Preparing for merge to the main branch. Will reenable on the branch”, a9914886da), and re-enabled after (2b91d96941, “turn GOEXPERIMENT=simd back on”). The unused internal/simd directory was deleted (62e1fccfb9). Helper commits: go/doc/comment must not list experimental packages in the std list (f045ed4110), generate.go tag (61a5a6b016), test helpers guarded with the amd64 tag so GOEXPERIMENT=simd go test simd/... works on other architectures (a5fe8c07ae), testdata subprocess tests set GOEXPERIMENT explicitly because Plan 9 does not inherit it (6d1bcd1009). A trial use inside the runtime (Green Tea GC scan kernels using SIMD: ~-19% geomean ScanSpanPacked, +25% throughput) was reverted before merge because “naming is confusing” plus a semantic merge conflict (da92168ec8, 0c69e77343).

Timeline.

Left open: experiment default off; simd name was reserved for a portable package.

  • Go 1.28 — Done: reverse merge 060245832f (2026-07-15); go.mod module path for simd/_gen repaired (db97d07dbb1.27); SVE reaches master (68f391a3c2). Left open: flag still off by default at HEAD (no commit changes this).

Portable simd package and the “midway” source translator

Span: Go 1.27 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: simd (vector-length-agnostic types Int8s..Float64s, Mask8s..Mask64s) exists behind GOEXPERIMENT=simd, implemented by rewriting user code in the compiler front end; the GODEBUG simd setting selects emulation and vector length.

Design. The package simd mirrors Highway: length-agnostic vectors whose width is bound at program run time. Its operations are declared with bodies that dispatch to simd/internal/bridge (types, tofrom_*.go conversions, per-arch decls_*.go, simd_emulated.go). The compiler package cmd/compile/internal/midway (“tiny-highway v0”, f1aa77c984) is a source-to-source translator run after type checking and before unified IR; to type-check the output it resets type info and re-runs the type checker. Phase 1 analysis finds functions, types, methods and variables that depend on simd types; “boundary” functions (simd-free signature but simd-using body) are rewritten into a dispatch function (original name) that chooses among specialised copies named with an @ suffix (illegal in Go identifiers, hence collision-free; methods are specialised by renaming their receiver type). rewriteSizes gives the variants per GOARCH (wasm {0,128}, amd64 {0,128,256,512}, arm64 {0,128}); size 0 means “emulated”. Non-boundary dependent functions are left in the export data with their bodies replaced by panic. The implementation relies on a builder hack to allow rewritten code to import the internal bridge package, and 90e20f8188 adds a hard dependence of simd types on the bridge package so go tools see the import.

Runtime selection: at startup simd checks that the hardware supports the assumed operation set for a vector width and downgrades (e.g. amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon has AVX2 but no 256-bit CLMUL, so it downgrades to 128-bit; NEON without PMULL such as Raspberry Pi gets an “arm64 nclm” variant that emulates only CLMUL, 8dd7aa0168). GODEBUG=simd=0 forces emulation, simd=N forces a length, simd=+N overrides the feature check (a92cf0ee94, which also adds HasVPCLMULQDQ to internal/cpu.X86). Benchmarks show the stakes: on an Apple laptop an inner-product kernel is -91% (arm64 128-bit), -93% (amd64 256), +594% under wasm-0 emulation vs the base (c82958326a); a 3-way CLMUL benchmark shows 2.3 ns SIMD vs 16 ns “clever” vs 67 ns iteration on arm64 (e873c5e929). Doc: ToArch(), Load<Types>Part, etc.

Timeline.

  • Go 1.27 — Done: user-visible first midway translator (f1aa77c984), arm64 support in midway (b7b03d9e3d), emulations (40eb69725e, 10231ce696, d7b3da6e25 rotates, edbc93f594 FP negation, cedf3d5870 unsigned OnesCount), CLMUL (cea3788e05), broadcast (b7327ecacf), GODEBUG switch (a92cf0ee94), shared type file (b2b5aa4d80), endianness test (c910146a98), docs and examples (c086c0e53b, c83d55f695), StorePart returns length (d2b991c840), HiToLo routed through Float64x2 (2458ba018e). Left open: BUG notes in doc.go: reflection calls, SIMD-dependent global var initializers, and modified names in stack traces do not work properly.
  • Go 1.28 — Done: user-visible architectural variation / “nclm” variant (8dd7aa0168), GODEBUG parsing fixes (30843789bf, 069f875c97), ReduceSum for floats and 8/16/32-bit ints (33c1f65079, 366d1805d1, ba7fdba26b), Load*Part no longer reads past the slice end (beaf715aaa), generated simd_emulated.go (c1db0bc3c4), copies-test (a58ac9ec4a). Left open: SVE-sized vectors (rewriteSizes comment: “this will change for SVE and cannot just be a size-based choice”).

ARM64 NEON archsimd

Span: Go 1.27 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: 128-bit NEON types and a large op set in ops_arm64.go; some constant shift ops postponed.

Design. Reuses the generic IsSIMD compiler plumbing and simdgen, but with a different instruction source (ARM ISA XML via 8437d1b188, arrangement symbols like 4S, 9764721859). Notable lowering tricks: upper-half “2” variants are not API; narrowing/widening are expressed by SSA folding of the lower-half base op with SetHi/GetHi (e.g. SHRN+SetHi -> SHRN2, XTN folded from SHRN shift 0, 6a8b351af9); shifts by vector or by a scalar ShiftAll use broadcast + SSHL/USHL with CSEL clamp for out-of-range amounts (39b11f4b14); Reduce* ops return a scalar via an unexported intrinsic plus GetElem(0) (8d29cf23b1); LookupOrZero (TBL) only for a single-register list (1768c11712; multi-register forms left as follow-ups). Ops added: arithmetic/rounding/min-max (c2f3871e15), shuffles (d2a9f4e364), saturating/pairwise/bit-count (3a6e136c90), bitwise (c473f30297), conversions (43df7ba2f5), comparisons and Masked/IfElse (ae7bac0a4b), MulAdd (555dd4691a), PMULL (627bc968ea), GetElem/SetElem (d62d649e1a), ConcatShiftBytesRight, horizontal reductions (da9cdfcbc0, f6490657e7), Broadcast (ae1c21739d), partial slice ops (399bc412ae), VCMTST peephole (62bb6b4a80), signed GetElem lowered to VSMOV (8db4546f29, with the assembler instruction b01fe21278).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.27 — Done: user-visible initial Add/Sub/Mul (8a1b0c8ecb), then the families above, test generator (61a10105e6), widening renamed LoLong->WidenLo (80ab7bc1fa). Release-trimming for 1.27: const-shift methods postponed (7de45e82f2), SetHi removed and GetHi renamed HiToLo (20e9fe5d36), LookupOrKeep removed (67c2e8b1fb), uint->mask conversions removed (07664b7a53), deprecated As... removed (9a23a318c9), Deinterleave/Transpose renamed (e50343d863), Reduce returns scalar (8d29cf23b1). Left open: multi-register TBL, const shifts needing rename.
  • Go 1.28 — Done: pairwise min/max, 64-bit-element Reduce, 8-bit ConcatAddPairs (77984f0ab4, ac2f54e4aa, 651ec67c3b), VCMTST (62bb6b4a80). Left open: nothing noted.

ARM64 SVE: scalable vectors and predicate masks

Span: Go 1.28 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: minimum-viable archsimd SVE types and a growing op set (types_sve.go, ops_sve.go); scalable vector length capped at 32 bytes in model, mask loads/stores removed.

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #79781 simd/archsimd: support ARM64 SVE SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT referenced by 18 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #73787 simd/archsimd: architecture-specific SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #79781

Design. SVE is an arm64 feature, not a GOARCH, but is treated as a fourth generation target. Scalable vectors are modelled as fixed 256-bit values (vector length bounded to 32 bytes at package init; mandatory panic for VL>32 later removed 75a79d1b6f), with LoadTPart/StorePart bounded by a runtime predicate (6fbc254146). The first MVP (68f391a3c2) plumbed types, ops and a test through the assembler. Predicate masks use the P registers: SVE predicate ops produce Mask types (fddf2d237d, first op Greater); Mask is a uint64 with one bit per vector byte (f662110644 removed LoadMask/Store because PSTR writes only VL/8 bytes). IfElse lowers to ZSEL, Masked is select against zero (4756f33d43); simdgen groups predicated and unpredicated encodings into one definition and folds a select over an unpredicated op into its merging form: (ZSELB (ZADDB x y) z mask) => (ZADDMergingPrefixedB z x y mask) with MOVPRFX. Predicated-only instructions (SMAX, UMAX, FMAX, ABS) run under an all-true predicate (PWHILELT, 6017e3eb32), and destructive ops use simdZ2kvPred which swaps sources or inserts unpredicated MOVPRFX (740fcaabb9). A correctness bug showed up at b6376b04a2: merging ops were marked commutative and not resultInArg0, so CSE merged x.Add(y).IfElse(m,x) and y.Add(x).IfElse(m,y) and returned the wrong lanes; fix is to mark merging ops resultInArg0 and non-commutative. Mask queries use PNEXT/PFIRST etc. (ad2488e65c: PNEXT with a false first operand since PFIRST has only a .B form; 7257a19fd5, 8a2ef7eb43, 9bdbfc8fa5, a90c4a7a58, 8dfdca7cf2 FromCount).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.28 — Done: user-visible MVP (68f391a3c2, e5da70bf01, 6fbc254146, fddf2d237d, 1a8b63dad2), IfElse/Masked (4756f33d43), arithmetic/compare/bitwise families (5b7fced4a3, 9de2d19c49, cc71e4955c, 76b21f0229, a9aed73003, 216cbea870, Sqrt/Ceil/Floor/Trunc/Round 978a95f616..5bcfe1bdd1, Equal/NotEqual/GreaterEqual 1dcfdf6fbf..2ba3d5f667, Max/Min/Div/MulAdd 740fcaabb9, bfc1e31771, 24fb3e7bc4, 8921b16049), ReduceSum/Max (dbd397ac6d, 387be25962), ShiftAllLeft (c72492ee6d), mask<->int (142236914f), SGEMM test with assembly baseline (2924f24765), SVE2 CPU detection (e077557cfb), RegMask widening. Left open: only a subset of SVE ops; predicate-register allocation bugs possible (RegisterSet fixed 966c78ed74); vector-length handling is fixed-256-bit model.

Spec-driven API generation (internal/spec, specgen, specfill)

Span: Go 1.28 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: in progress; simd/internal/spec is an executable Go specification of all possible SIMD operations, with specgen, specls, refgen, specfill, specstats tools; plan tracked in SPEC-TRANSITION.md.

Design docs & discussion
  • tracking issue #81819 simd: unify API generation around executable spec referenced by 11 of this thread's commits
  • proposal #78902 simd: architecture and vector-size agnostic SIMD intrinsics under a GOEXPERIMENT linked from #81819

Design. Problem: the same operation was described in six places that drifted. spec describes each operation once as a generic Go function over Vec[E, W] (element class constraint such as Nums, width W = 128/256/512/scalable), giving signature, doc and executable semantics; specgen (with a constraint solver specexpr, 2eb6506ad7) expands it into concrete methods, refgen produces a reference implementation (simdref, 26fee28ba5) for conformance testing, and specfill injects spec docs and parameter/result names into generated and hand-written source and verifies signatures (73adfe029b, d73c92c091). It is intended to replace categories.yaml (810fe52b24). The “one meaning” rule (a name means one thing across arch, types and both packages) is the guiding invariant (README). Conformance testing found real bugs: FMA (958aac0d81), KANDN order (e2889b0bf5), integer Div (6acc64e461). spec was moved up the package DAG because the vectors are slices and allocate, so it cannot serve as a runtime-importable emulation (5b8216128d).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.28 — Done: initial spec (810fe52b24), generator (aa7b8a796d), specls (9704c21b22), refgen, categories and commutativity (251583b606), shifts (f081a1ab32), docs filled from spec (ede51d4986, 9450dc4b55), name filling (d9c017a1fa, 021b49fbb9), host feature audit (1fe66956c2), “simd-common” done (b6680141e6), ScaleSaturated rename (299a042625), parameter-name reconciliation (c35d7bdf94, 5d8f28c94d). Left open: retire categories.yaml, behavioural conformance beyond mathlib tests; impl-defined behaviour (“allowed wiggle room is not yet well-defined”).

API shaping and renames before stabilisation

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: API still experimental; renames continue.

Design docs & discussion
  • proposal #76473 simd: rename low-level SIMD package to simd/archsimd (GOEXPERIMENT) linked from #78979

The public API was repeatedly adjusted for consistency: reordered operands (ead249a2e2/55665e1e37), Shift*AndFillUpperFrom->Shift*Concat (2c25f3e846), DotProd->DotProduct, AES/SHA op names (0978935a99, be9c50c6a0), conversion names (3fdd183aef), loads/stores “scalable first” (b70242b3b9: LoadT->LoadTArray, LoadTSlice->LoadT, Store->StoreArray), RoundToEven->Round (9bc619add4), AddSub->AddOddSubEven (35ea327859), SumAbsDiff->SumOf8AbsDiff (8583ef15c8), TruncateToX->TruncToX (3e04a409d1), all shifts/rotates take uint64 (fed139a1b3), MulEvenWiden->MulWidenEven (3521c10d5e), SaturateToConcat->ConcatSaturateTo (23761e7bb2), As conversions deprecated for factored templates (3d6c5301df). Emulation of missing instructions and test infrastructure

Span: Go 1.26 → Go 1.28 · Status at HEAD: ops_emulated_*.go per arch; generated test helpers.

Design. Where an operation is not a single instruction on some CPU level, archsimd provides a pure-Go emulation built from vector ops (Not, AVX2 comparisons 2080415aa2, bitwise ops 94d72355f6, rotate-from-shifts d7b3da6e25, FP negation edbc93f594, OnesCount for bytes 385f272158, ReduceSum). Tests are generated with generics (88568519b4), the internal tests do not import testing into simd (95b4ad525f), tests deduplicated across architectures (c554c53ac8..b350da230f), and test-gate and helper packages simd/internal/test_helpers (dd22b9816b). Benchmarks: inner-product kernels (c82958326a) and transposes (1c961c2fb2).

Timeline.

  • Go 1.26 — Done: 94d72355f6, 2080415aa2, be57d94c4c (Not), 88568519b4. Left open: emulations named “wrong name” first.
